definition_zh: 复印件；影印件；复印；影印
definition_en: a copy of a page or picture made by a machine that scans the original and prints it again; to make such a copy
core_image: 绿灯从纸页下面扫过，原件旁边立刻多出一张几乎一样的纸
scene: 出入境大厅的窗口前，办事员把护照放到玻璃板上，按下按钮。The clerk made a photocopy of my passport and handed it back with the receipt.
sceneCN: 这里是「复印件」（第 1 个义项：机器复制出来的纸本）；句意为办事员复印了我的护照，连同收据一起递还。图中的玻璃板、亮起的扫描条和吐出的纸页正是复印机的动作。

derivatives.zh: photocopy 去 y 加 -er，指执行复印这件事的机器，义为「复印机」
photocopy 加 -ing，把动作变成过程名词，义为「复印；复印业务」
photocopy 加 -able，义为「可以复印的」，教材上常见

senses.title: A machine-made copy of a page
senses.definition: a copy of a document or picture produced by a machine that scans the original and prints the same image again
senses.definitionCN: 用机器扫描原件、再把同样的图像印出来而得到的文件或图片副本
senses.example: Keep a photocopy of the contract in the drawer.
senses.exampleCN: 把合同的复印件放在抽屉里。
senses.why: Photo- adds the idea of an image and copy adds the Latin sense of one more unit, so the machine never writes anything new; it multiplies an existing image onto a second sheet.
senses.whyCN: photo- 带来「影像」，copy 的拉丁本义是「多出一份」，所以复印机并不写新内容，只是把已有的影像再放到一张纸上，让它多出一份。

senses.title: To reproduce a page by machine
senses.definition: to make a copy of a document or picture with a copying machine
senses.definitionCN: 用复印机复制文件或图片
senses.example: Could you photocopy these pages before the meeting?
senses.exampleCN: 你能在开会前把这些页面复印一下吗？
senses.why: English turns product nouns into verbs without any suffix, so the same spelling names both the sheet on the tray and the act that put it there.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把指成品的名词直接用作动词，不加词尾；于是同一个拼写既指托盘里的那张纸，也指把它做出来的那个动作。

intro.en: Photocopy joins a Greek element for light to a Latin word for plenty; the machine later changed its chemistry while the old name stayed.
intro.cn: photocopy 把希腊语表示「光」的成分和拉丁语表示「充足」的词接在一起；后来机器的成像原理换了，名字却留了下来。

items.en: Phos, with the genitive photos, meant light, and the combining form photo- was already used by nineteenth-century science for things produced by light.
items.cn: phos 的属格是 photos，意为光；photo- 这个组合形式在十九世纪科学里已用来指由光产生的东西。

items.en: Copia meant abundance and supply; through Old French copie it became English copy, one more unit of a text.
items.cn: copia 意为充足、供应；经古法语 copie 进入英语成为 copy，指文本多出来的一份。

items.en: Photo- and copy were joined in English for a reproduction made by a photographic process, at first a photograph of a page.
items.cn: 英语把 photo- 与 copy 拼合，指用照相工艺做出的复制品，最初就是一页文件的照片。

items.en: When office machines could expose paper to light and fix toner on it, the same word moved to the plain-paper copy people still make today.
items.cn: 当办公机器能让纸张曝光并把墨粉固定上去，同一个词就转指今天仍在制作的普通纸复印件。

items.en: Photocopy now covers the paper and the act, while photocopier names the machine and photocopying names the service.
items.cn: 现代英语里 photocopy 兼指纸本与动作，photocopier 指机器，photocopying 指这项业务。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the two halves of the word, Greek photo- and Latin copy; the near-meaning group collects other words for a second version of a page.
note.cn: 形近组沿着这个词的两半展开，希腊语的 photo- 与拉丁语的 copy；近义组收其他表示「纸页的第二份」的词。

entries.definition: The machine that does the copying, built with -er on the same base.
entries.definitionCN: 执行复印的机器，在同一词干上加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: The process or service of reproducing pages, marked by -ing.
entries.definitionCN: 复制纸页的过程或业务，由 -ing 标记。

entries.definition: A camera picture made by light; it shares photo- but ends in the Greek -graph, not in copy.
entries.definitionCN: 用相机拍下、由光成像的画面；同用 photo-，结尾却是希腊语的 -graph，不是 copy。

entries.definition: One duplicate of a text or image, the Latin half that photocopy carries.
entries.definitionCN: 文本或图像的一份副本，是 photocopy 所带的拉丁语那一半。

entries.definition: An exact second version of something that already exists.
entries.definitionCN: 已有事物完全一样的第二份。

entries.definition: A copy of an image or text, often made for printing or display.
entries.definitionCN: 图像或文本的复制品，常为印刷或展示而做。

entries.definition: A page a printer produces from a computer file rather than from a paper original.
entries.definitionCN: 打印机从电脑文件而非纸质原件输出的一页。

entries.definition: To turn a page into a digital image, the step that often comes before copies are made.
entries.definitionCN: 把纸页变成数字图像，常是复制之前的步骤。

normalIntro.en: The word is built from two real halves, and each half explains part of what the machine does.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由两个真实的成分拼成，每一半都解释了机器所做事情的一部分。

normal.en: Photo- gives the image and copy gives the extra one, so a photocopy is an image that has been multiplied.
normal.cn: photo- 给出影像，copy 给出多出来的一份，所以 photocopy 就是被复制了一份的影像。

normal.en: The machine, not the person, is the photocopier: -er here marks a device, as it does in printer and scanner.
normal.cn: 机器而不是人才是 photocopier：这里的 -er 标记器械，和 printer、scanner 一样。

normal.en: Photocopying keeps -ing for the activity, so a photocopying service sells the act, not the paper.
normal.cn: photocopying 用 -ing 表示活动，所以复印服务卖的是这项动作，而不是纸张。

normal.en: Modern machines use toner and static electricity, but light still exposes the page, so the photo- half is not a lie.
normal.cn: 现代机器用墨粉和静电，但纸页仍靠光曝光，所以 photo- 那一半并没有说谎。

normal.en: Photocopy has no -graph: its second half is Latin copy, which is exactly what separates it from photograph.
normal.cn: photocopy 没有 -graph：后半截是拉丁语 copy，这正是它与 photograph 的分界。

abstract.en: A photocopy is a stand-in that can be read, filed and lost without anyone touching the original.
abstract.cn: 复印件是一个替身：它可以被阅读、归档、遗失，而原件始终无人碰过。

abstract.en: The name still promises light although the machine mostly moves powder, which is how words quietly age.
abstract.cn: 名字仍在承诺「光」，机器却主要在搬运粉末，词语就是这样悄悄老去的。

abstract.en: Two identical pages raise a small question: which one is the document and which one is only a trace of it.
abstract.cn: 两张一样的纸会引出一个问题：哪一张是文件本身，哪一张只是它的痕迹。

examples.en: Keep a photocopy of the contract in the drawer.
examples.cn: 把合同的复印件放在抽屉里。

examples.en: Could you photocopy these pages before the meeting?
examples.cn: 你能在开会前把这些页面复印一下吗？

examples.en: She photocopied the whole file twice.
examples.cn: 她把整份档案复印了两遍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「否头拷皮」——把原件的外皮拷一份到新纸上；记住 photocopy 是复印件，也能当动词「复印」。

root: 希腊语 phos/photos（光）+ 拉丁语 copia（充足、副本，经古法语 copie 入英语）；photo- 只借了「光」，后半截 copy 并非希腊语 -graph。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a second copy produced through an image-forming machine; the senses divide only by whether the word names the paper or the act.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是通过成像机器多出来的一份副本；两个义项只在于是指那张纸，还是指复印这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bar of green light sliding under a page while an identical sheet slides out below.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道绿光从纸页下扫过，下面同时滑出另一张一模一样的纸。

branches.en: a passport copy folded into a coat pocket
branches.cn: 折进外套口袋的护照复印件

branches.en: a hand pressing the copy button twice
branches.cn: 一只手连按两下复印键

branches.en: the act ending in a warm stack of paper
branches.cn: 动作结束于一叠还带着温度的纸

branches.en: a class handout identical to the teacher's page
branches.cn: 与老师那页一模一样的课堂讲义

branches.en: copying a whole file before a meeting
branches.cn: 开会前把整份档案复印一遍

intro.en: The word stands on a Greek element for light and a Latin noun for plenty, and English welds them without a linking vowel change.
intro.cn: 这个词站在希腊语表示「光」的成分和拉丁语表示「充足」的名词上，英语把两者直接焊在一起。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: a machine-made copy; to make one

definition_zh: 照片；相片；拍照；拍摄
definition_en: a picture made with a camera, in which light is recorded on film or a sensor; to take such a picture
core_image: 快门一响，一小片光被钉在纸上，成了可以拿在手里的画面
scene: 老式相机架在木架上，摄影师让孩子别动，等光刚好落在脸上。She photographed the whole street before the rain came.
sceneCN: 这里是「拍照」（第 2 个义项：用相机记录）；句意为她在下雨之前把整条街拍了下来。木架、黑布和等待光线的孩子都指向「按下快门」这个动作。

derivatives.zh: photograph 换 -ic 词尾，义为「摄影的；与摄影有关的」
photo- 加 -graphy，义为「摄影术」；-graphy 指书写、记录的过程，与 -graph 的成品相对
photograph 加 -er，义为「摄影师」；同一词干上 -er 专门指人
photo- 加 -genic（产生），义为「上相的；适合拍照的」

senses.title: A picture made by light
senses.definition: a picture formed when light from a scene is recorded on film or on a sensor inside a camera
senses.definitionCN: 相机把景物反射的光记录在胶片或传感器上而形成的画面
senses.example: He kept a photograph of his grandparents on the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 他在书桌上放着一张祖父母的照片。
senses.why: The Greek elements say light writing, so the object is literally what light wrote on a surface; English named the finished result before it named the act of making it.
senses.whyCN: 两个希腊成分合起来是「用光书写」，照片就是光在表面上写下的东西；英语先给这个成品命名，再给制作它的动作命名。

senses.title: To take a picture with a camera
senses.definition: to take a picture of a person, place or event with a camera
senses.definitionCN: 用相机把人、地点或事件拍成照片
senses.example: She photographed the whole street before the rain came.
senses.exampleCN: 她在下雨前拍下了整条街。
senses.why: English lets a product noun become a verb with no ending at all; photograph, copy and film all travel this zero-conversion path, so noun and verb sound identical.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许指成品的名词不加词尾直接变成动词；photograph、copy、film 都走这条零转换的路，所以名词和动词读音完全相同。

senses.title: To come out in a certain way in pictures
senses.titleCN: 上相；在照片里呈现某种样子
senses.definition: to appear in photographs in a particular way, especially attractively
senses.definitionCN: 在照片里呈现出某种样子，尤指好看、上镜
senses.example: That dark blue coat photographs well in winter light.
senses.exampleCN: 那件深蓝色外套在冬日光线里很上相。
senses.why: Once the verb means to record, it can also judge the record: the subject, not the camera operator, is being assessed for how it looks on film, which is why the adverb well fits so naturally.
senses.whyCN: 动词一旦表示「记录下来」，就能评判记录的效果：被评估的是被拍对象在照片里的样子，而不是拍摄者的技术，所以 well 这个副词用在这里特别自然。

intro.en: Photograph is a nineteenth-century coinage from two Greek words, and its three endings -graph, -grapher and -graphy settled into English within a few years of one another.
intro.cn: photograph 是十九世纪用两个希腊词造出来的新词；-graph、-grapher、-graphy 三种结尾在英语里几乎同时定型。

items.en: Phos, whose genitive is photos, meant light and supplied the combining form photo-.
items.cn: phos 的属格是 photos，意为光，提供了组合形式 photo-。

items.en: Graphein meant to scratch, carve, draw or write, and the noun graphe meant a drawing or a piece of writing.
items.cn: graphein 意为刻、雕、画、写，名词 graphe 指图画或文字。

items.en: French and German writers formed photographie for the new light-made image, and Sir John Herschel is usually credited with the English photograph in 1839.
items.cn: 法国和德国的作者为新出现的感光影像造出 photographie；一般认为英语的 photograph 由约翰·赫歇尔在 1839 年确定。

items.en: English fixed -graph for the image, -er for the person and -y for the practice, all on the same Greek base, which is why the family looks so regular.
items.cn: 英语用同一希腊词干固定了三种结尾：-graph 指影像，-er 指人，-y 指技艺，所以这一族词看起来格外整齐。

items.en: The verb came by conversion, and the clipped photo took over everyday speech while photograph stayed in captions, labels and technical writing.
items.cn: 动词由名词零转换而来；口语里由 photo 这个截短形式承担，photograph 则留在图注、标签和技术文字中。

note.en: The look-alike group shows how the same Greek base changes its ending for object, person, adjective and practice; the near-meaning group collects other names for a camera image.
note.cn: 形近组展示同一希腊词干如何靠不同结尾分别指物、指人、指性质、指技艺；近义组收其他表示「相机影像」的词。

entries.definition: The art or process of making photographs; -graphy names the practice, not the object.
entries.definitionCN: 拍摄照片的技艺或过程；-graphy 指做法，不指物件。

entries.definition: The person who takes photographs; -er marks the human agent.
entries.definitionCN: 拍照的人；-er 标记施动的人。

entries.definition: Relating to photography, or able to record light chemically or electronically.
entries.definitionCN: 与摄影有关的，或能以化学、电子方式记录光的。

entries.definition: A machine-made copy of a page; it borrows photo- but its second half is Latin copy, not the Greek -graph.
entries.definitionCN: 机器复制出的一页副本；借了 photo-，后半却是拉丁语 copy，不是希腊语 -graph。

entries.definition: A visual image of any kind, painted, drawn or taken with a camera.
entries.definitionCN: 任何形式的视觉图像，画的、绘的或拍的。

entries.definition: A visible representation, often used for what appears on a screen or in the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 可见的呈现，常用于屏幕上的画面或心中的形象。

entries.definition: A quick, informal picture taken without much preparation.
entries.definitionCN: 随手拍下、不做多少准备的快照。

entries.definition: A photograph or painting of a person, usually centred on the face.
entries.definitionCN: 人物照片或画像，通常以脸为中心。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Greek sentence compressed into a compound, and its endings tell you whether you are holding the thing, the person or the craft.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是把一句希腊语压成复合词，它的结尾告诉你手里拿的是东西、是人，还是手艺。

normal.en: Photo- is light and -graph is what is written or drawn, so a photograph is light's drawing.
normal.cn: photo- 是光，-graph 是被写下、被画出的东西，所以 photograph 就是光的画。

normal.en: -graph gives the thing, -grapher gives the person, -graphy gives the practice: three endings, three jobs.
normal.cn: -graph 给出实物，-grapher 给出人，-graphy 给出技艺：三种结尾，三种分工。

normal.en: The verb photograph adds nothing to the noun; English simply uses the thing-word as an action-word.
normal.cn: 动词 photograph 没有加任何词尾；英语直接把指物的词拿来指动作。

normal.en: Photograph well judges how the subject looks in pictures, not how skilled the person holding the camera is.
normal.cn: photograph well 评判的是被拍对象在照片里的样子，不是持相机者的技术。

normal.en: In speech photo does most of the work, while photograph belongs to captions, forms and formal description.
normal.cn: 口语里多由 photo 承担，photograph 则出现在图注、表格和正式描述中。

abstract.en: A photograph is light that was stopped and taught to stay on a surface.
abstract.cn: 照片是被拦下来的光，被教会停在某个表面上。

abstract.en: The word splits the world into light and writing, which is why a good picture can feel like a sentence.
abstract.cn: 这个词把世界分成「光」与「书写」，所以一张好照片读起来像一句话。

abstract.en: Every photograph is also a decision about what was left outside the frame.
abstract.cn: 每张照片同时也是一次决定：决定把什么留在画框之外。

examples.en: He kept a photograph of his grandparents on the desk.
examples.cn: 他在书桌上放着一张祖父母的照片。

examples.en: She photographed the whole street before the rain came.
examples.cn: 她在下雨前拍下了整条街。

examples.en: That dark blue coat photographs well in winter light.
examples.cn: 那件深蓝色外套在冬日光线里很上相。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「否头格拉夫」——光在纸上写下的一格画面；记住 photograph 是照片，也能当动词「拍照」。

root: 希腊语 phos/photos（光）+ graphein（刻、画、写），合成「用光写下的东西」；-graph 指写下的成品，-grapher 指写的人，-graphy 指写的过程或技艺。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an image written by light; the noun names the image, the verb names the act, and the third sense judges how a subject comes out in the image.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是由光写成的画面；名词指画面，动词指拍摄动作，第三个义项则评判被拍对象在画面里呈现得如何。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shutter opening for a fraction of a second while light burns a small image onto a surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：快门只开了一瞬，光在表面上烙下一小块画面。

branches.en: a framed picture standing on a desk
branches.cn: 立在书桌上的带框照片

branches.en: a hand lifting a camera in the rain
branches.cn: 雨中举起相机的手

branches.en: a coat that looks better on film than in the room
branches.cn: 在照片里比在屋里更好看的外套

branches.en: the picture and the act that produced it
branches.cn: 照片与拍出它的那个动作

branches.en: a face kept after the person has gone
branches.cn: 人已离开却留在纸上的脸

intro.en: The compound is Greek on both sides, and English added the endings that split the family into object, person and practice.
intro.cn: 这个复合词两半都来自希腊语，英语再加上不同结尾，把这一族分成物、人和技艺。

latinIntro.en: The root is Greek, and no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词的词根是希腊语，没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 摄影师；拍照的人
definition_en: a person who takes photographs, especially as a job or as an art
core_image: 一个人半蹲在路边，相机贴在眼前，等那只鸟起飞
scene: 婚礼现场人来人往，一个背着两台相机的人在人群里挪动脚步，寻找角度。The photographer waved the family into the last patch of sunlight.
sceneCN: 这里是「摄影师」（第 1 个义项：以拍照为职业的人）；句意为摄影师招手让一家人站到最后那一小块阳光里。背着的相机和寻找角度的动作都指向这个职业身份。

derivatives.zh: photographer 去掉 -er 换 -y，义为「摄影术」；-grapher 指人，-graphy 指技艺
photograph 加 -ic，义为「摄影的」
photo- 加 -genic（产生），义为「上相的」

senses.title: A person who takes pictures for a living
senses.definition: a person who takes photographs, especially someone who does it as a job
senses.definitionCN: 拍摄照片的人，尤指以此为职业者
senses.example: The photographer waved the family into the last patch of sunlight.
senses.exampleCN: 摄影师招手让一家人站到最后一小块阳光里。
senses.why: -er selects the human agent out of the whole act of photographing, so the word names a role rather than a single click of the shutter.
senses.whyCN: -er 从整个拍摄行为里挑出「施动的人」，所以这个词指的是一个角色，而不是某一次按下快门。

senses.title: The person credited for one particular picture
senses.definition: the person who took a particular picture, often named in a credit line
senses.definitionCN: 拍下某张特定照片的人，常在署名中注明
senses.example: The credit line lists her as the photographer of the cover image.
senses.exampleCN: 版权署名把她列为封面照片的拍摄者。
senses.why: The same role word can be pinned to one image: a credit line turns a profession into a signature, which is why the definite article often appears.
senses.whyCN: 同一个表示角色的词也能固定到某一幅影像上：署名把职业变成签名，所以这里常带定冠词。

intro.en: Photographer was coined alongside photograph in 1839, once -er was added to the new word for a light-made image.
intro.cn: photographer 与 photograph 同在 1839 年前后被造出，做法是在这个表示感光影像的新词后加 -er。

items.en: Phos, genitive photos, meant light and gave the first element of the new compound.
items.cn: phos 的属格是 photos，意为光，提供了这个新复合词的第一部分。

items.en: Graphein meant to draw or write, and the Greek combining form -graphos already named one who writes or draws.
items.cn: graphein 意为画、写，希腊语的组合成分 -graphos 本来就指书写或描画的人。

items.en: Sir John Herschel is usually credited with photograph, photography and photographer in the same year, when the new process needed names for the image, the craft and the worker.
items.cn: 一般认为 photograph、photography、photographer 都由约翰·赫歇尔在同一年确定；当时这项新工艺正需要给影像、技艺和操作者分别命名。

items.en: English -er marked the doer, so photographer named the person while -graph stayed on the object and -y went to the practice.
items.cn: 英语的 -er 标记施动者，于是 photographer 指人，-graph 留在物件上，-y 则归到技艺。

items.en: The word now covers staff photographers, freelancers and hobbyists, and compounds such as photojournalist build on it.
items.cn: 现代英语里它既指机构摄影师，也指自由职业者和爱好者，photojournalist 这类复合词也建在它上面。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the same Greek family, with the ending showing which member is meant; the near-meaning group collects other camera workers and image makers.
note.cn: 形近组收同一希腊词族的成员，靠结尾区分所指；近义组收其他与相机、影像打交道的人。

entries.definition: The image itself, ending in -graph rather than in -er.
entries.definitionCN: 影像本身，结尾是 -graph 而不是 -er。

entries.definition: The art or trade, ending in -graphy instead of naming a person.
entries.definitionCN: 摄影的技艺或行业，结尾是 -graphy，不指人。

entries.definition: The adjective for anything relating to the making of photographs.
entries.definitionCN: 表示与拍摄照片有关的形容词。

entries.definition: A photographer who reports news through pictures.
entries.definitionCN: 用照片报道新闻的摄影师。

entries.definition: A person who operates a camera, especially for film or television.
entries.definitionCN: 操作摄影机的人，尤指影视拍摄。

entries.definition: The person responsible for the camera and lighting of a film.
entries.definitionCN: 负责一部电影摄影与布光的人。

entries.definition: A person who makes art, including someone whose photographs are shown as art.
entries.definitionCN: 从事艺术创作的人，包括把照片作为艺术展出的人。

normalIntro.en: The word is a job title built by suffix, and its neighbours show exactly which suffix does which job.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是靠后缀搭出来的职业名称，它的同族词正好显示每个后缀各管什么。

normal.en: Photographer is photograph plus -er, and -er points at the person who performs the action.
normal.cn: photographer 就是 photograph 加 -er，而 -er 指向执行动作的人。

normal.en: The family divides neatly: -graph the picture, -grapher the person, -graphy the practice.
normal.cn: 这一族分得很清楚：-graph 是照片，-grapher 是人，-graphy 是技艺。

normal.en: Greek -graphos already meant one who writes or draws, so -grapher repeats an old idea in English spelling.
normal.cn: 希腊语 -graphos 本来就指书写或描画的人，所以 -grapher 只是用英语拼写重复了一个旧概念。

normal.en: A press photographer works to a deadline; a wedding photographer works to a family's memory, but both carry the same -er.
normal.cn: 新闻摄影师赶截稿时间，婚礼摄影师对着一家人的记忆工作，但两者都带同一个 -er。

normal.en: A photo credit is simply the place where this -er word is printed under the image.
normal.cn: 照片署名无非是把带 -er 的这个词印在影像下方。

abstract.en: The photographer stands between the world and the picture, deciding what the rest of us will see.
abstract.cn: 摄影师站在世界与照片之间，替其余的人决定可以看到什么。

abstract.en: The person who spends a life behind a lens is often the one missing from the family album.
abstract.cn: 常年站在镜头后的人，往往正是家庭相册里缺席的那一个。

abstract.en: The suffix is small but decisive: without -er there is only an image, with it there is a witness.
abstract.cn: 这个后缀很小却很关键：没有 -er 只有一张影像，有了它就有了一个见证者。

examples.en: The photographer waved the family into the last patch of sunlight.
examples.cn: 摄影师招手让一家人站到最后一小块阳光里。

examples.en: She hired a photographer for the opening night.
examples.cn: 她为开幕之夜请了一位摄影师。

examples.en: Press photographers waited outside the court all morning.
examples.cn: 新闻摄影师在法院外等了一上午。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「否头格拉弗」——把光写下来的人；记住 photographer 是摄影师，结尾 -er 专指人。

root: 希腊语 phos/photos（光）+ graphein（写、画）+ 英语 -er（人）；同一词干上 -graph 是成品，-grapher 是人，-graphy 是技艺。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the person who operates the camera; the two senses split between the job and the name attached to one particular picture.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是操作相机的人；两个义项分别指这份职业，以及某一幅具体照片的署名者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure kneeling on the pavement, one eye behind the camera, waiting for the exact second.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人跪在人行道上，一只眼睛贴在相机后，等那个准确的瞬间。

branches.en: a wedding photographer stepping between the tables
branches.cn: 在餐桌间穿行的婚礼摄影师

branches.en: a press photographer waiting behind the police line
branches.cn: 警戒线后等待的新闻摄影师

branches.en: a name printed in small type under a cover image
branches.cn: 封面图下小字印着的名字

branches.en: the same name as a job and as an author
branches.cn: 同一个名字既是职业也是作者

branches.en: a low angle taken from one knee
branches.cn: 单膝跪地拍出的低角度

intro.en: The word is the meeting point of three formatives, and the last one decides that a person, not a picture or a craft, is meant.
intro.cn: 这个词是三个构词成分的交汇处，最后一个成分决定了它指人，而不是指照片或技艺。

latinIntro.en: The root is Greek, and no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词的词根是希腊语，没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: turns the person-word into the practice-word
items.meaningCN: 把指人的词变成指技艺的词

definition_zh: 摄影术；摄影；摄影业
definition_en: the art, process or business of taking and producing photographs
core_image: 暗房的红灯下，一张白纸在药水里慢慢浮出树影
scene: 暗房里只有一盏红灯，夹子把湿漉漉的相纸从药水里提起来，树影一点点显出来。Photography began as chemistry before it became an art.
sceneCN: 这里是「摄影术」（第 1 个义项：拍摄与成像的技艺）；句意为摄影在成为艺术之前，先是一门化学。红灯、药水和慢慢显影的相纸正是这门技艺的现场。

derivatives.zh: photo- 加 -graph 再加 -er，义为「摄影师」；与 -graphy 只差一个结尾
photograph 加 -ic，义为「摄影的」
photo- 加 -genic（产生），义为「上相的」
astro-（星）加 photography，义为「天文摄影」

senses.title: The art and process of making images with light
senses.definition: the art and process of recording images by the action of light on film or on a sensor
senses.definitionCN: 利用光在胶片或传感器上成像、从而记录画面的技艺与过程
senses.example: Photography began as chemistry before it became an art.
senses.exampleCN: 摄影在成为艺术之前，先是一门化学。
senses.why: -graphy names a practice rather than a thing: the same Greek base that gives the picture also gives the skill of making pictures once the ending shifts to -y.
senses.whyCN: -graphy 指一种做法而不是一件东西：同一个希腊词干，结尾换成 -y，就从「照片」变成「拍照片的技艺」。

senses.title: The trade built on that practice
senses.definition: the business or activity of producing photographs, especially for clients or publications
senses.definitionCN: 为客户或出版物拍摄、制作照片的行业或活动
senses.example: She moved to Milan to work in fashion photography.
senses.exampleCN: 她搬到米兰从事时尚摄影。
senses.why: Abstract craft nouns regularly extend to the trade that lives off them, and photography followed printing and painting along the same path.
senses.whyCN: 表示技艺的抽象名词常会扩展到靠它吃饭的行当；photography 沿着 printing、painting 走过的同一条路延伸。

intro.en: Photography names a practice, and its history runs from a Greek suffix for writing through a French coinage of the 1830s to a global industry.
intro.cn: photography 命名一门技艺，它的历史从希腊语表示「书写」的后缀，经十九世纪三十年代的法语新造词，一直走到今天的全球行业。

items.en: Phos, genitive photos, meant light and supplied the first element of the compound.
items.cn: phos 的属格是 photos，意为光，提供了复合词的第一部分。

items.en: Graphein meant to draw or write; the derived noun graphia named a writing, a drawing or a record.
items.cn: graphein 意为画、写；由它派生的名词 graphia 指书写、图画或记录。

items.en: Hercules Florence used photographie in 1834, and the word spread with the processes that Daguerre and Talbot made public in 1839.
items.cn: 埃尔屈勒·弗洛朗斯在 1834 年使用了 photographie；随着达盖尔与塔尔博特在 1839 年公布新工艺，这个词传播开来。

items.en: English kept -graph for the image, -er for the person and -y for the practice, a division that still explains the whole family.
items.cn: 英语保留 -graph 指影像、-er 指人、-y 指技艺，这个分工至今仍能解释整族词。

items.en: Digital sensors replaced film, but photography still covers the art, the course of study and the industry, with compounds such as astrophotography extending it.
items.cn: 数码传感器取代了胶片，但 photography 仍兼指艺术、学科与行业，astrophotography 这类复合词继续扩展它的范围。

note.en: The look-alike group lines up the same Greek family so the endings can be compared; the near-meaning group collects other crafts that produce images.
note.cn: 形近组把同一希腊词族的成员排在一起，便于比较结尾；近义组收其他生产影像的技艺。

entries.definition: One image, ending in -graph; the practice word ends in -y instead.
entries.definitionCN: 一张影像，结尾是 -graph；指技艺的词结尾则是 -y。

entries.definition: The person who practises it, ending in -er.
entries.definitionCN: 从事这门技艺的人，结尾是 -er。

entries.definition: The adjective describing materials, methods or effects of the craft.
entries.definitionCN: 描述这门技艺的材料、方法或效果的形容词。

entries.definition: Likely to look good in a photograph, built with -genic.
entries.definitionCN: 适合上镜、拍照好看的，由 -genic 构成。

entries.definition: The craft of photographing films, where -graphy also names a technique.
entries.definitionCN: 电影拍摄的技艺；这里的 -graphy 同样指一门技术。

entries.definition: The way a camera is used in a film or television programme.
entries.definitionCN: 影视作品中运用摄影机的方式。

entries.definition: The technical process of producing images, especially digital ones.
entries.definitionCN: 生成图像的技术过程，尤指数字成像。

normalIntro.en: The word is a practice noun, and its -graphy ending is the same one that turns other roots into crafts and fields of study.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是表示技艺的名词，它的 -graphy 结尾与把其他词根变成手艺、学科时用的是同一个。

normal.en: -graphy comes from Greek -graphia, a writing or a record, so photography is writing with light.
normal.cn: -graphy 来自希腊语 -graphia，意为书写或记录，所以 photography 就是用光书写。

normal.en: -graph is the picture, -grapher the person, -graphy the practice; only the last letters change.
normal.cn: -graph 是照片，-grapher 是人，-graphy 是技艺；变的只是最后几个字母。

normal.en: The -y ending makes an uncountable noun of a skill, as it does in geography and calligraphy.
normal.cn: -y 结尾把技能变成不可数名词，geography 和 calligraphy 也是这样。

normal.en: Photography covers both the art and the industry, so a photography course can lead to a photography business.
normal.cn: photography 兼指艺术与行业，所以摄影课程可以通向一门摄影生意。

normal.en: Digital sensors replaced film, but a sensor still counts light, so the photo- half remains accurate.
normal.cn: 数码传感器取代了胶片，但传感器仍在计量光，所以 photo- 那一半依然准确。

abstract.en: Photography is a bargain with time: it keeps a moment but never the moment itself.
abstract.cn: 摄影是与时间做的一笔交易：它留住一个瞬间，却从不是那个瞬间本身。

abstract.en: -graphy turns an action into a discipline, which is why the word sounds like something you can study.
abstract.cn: -graphy 把动作变成一门学科，所以这个词听起来像可以选修的科目。

abstract.en: A craft named after light and writing keeps both halves visible every time a print appears in the tray.
abstract.cn: 一门以光与书写命名的技艺，每次相纸在托盘里显影，都让这两半同时可见。

examples.en: Photography began as chemistry before it became an art.
examples.cn: 摄影在成为艺术之前，先是一门化学。

examples.en: She moved to Milan to work in fashion photography.
examples.cn: 她搬到米兰从事时尚摄影。

examples.en: Digital photography made the darkroom optional but not extinct.
examples.cn: 数码摄影让暗房不再是必需，却没有让它消失。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「否头格拉菲」——用光写字的手艺；记住 photography 是摄影术，结尾 -graphy 指技艺。

root: 希腊语 phos/photos（光）+ graphein（写）+ 希腊名词后缀 -ia（英语作 -y）；-graph 指成品，-grapher 指人，-graphy 指书写、记录的技艺。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the practice of writing with light; one sense names the art and process, the other the trade that grew out of it.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是用光书写的技艺；一个义项指这门艺术与过程，另一个指由它生长出来的行业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a print rising out of a tray of developer under a red darkroom lamp.
core.cn: 核心意象：暗房红灯下，一张相纸从显影液里慢慢浮出画面。

branches.en: a red lamp over a tray of developer
branches.cn: 显影液上方的一盏红灯

branches.en: a student learning exposure in a first course
branches.cn: 入门课上练习曝光的学生

branches.en: a studio booking a shoot for a fashion brand
branches.cn: 为时尚品牌安排拍摄的摄影棚

branches.en: an amateur habit turning into a paid trade
branches.cn: 从业余爱好变成收费行当

branches.en: pages of a magazine paid for by the shoot
branches.cn: 杂志上由这次拍摄换来的版面

intro.en: The word combines a Greek element for light with the Greek suffix for a craft, and the same suffix organises the whole family.
intro.cn: 这个词把希腊语表示「光」的成分与表示技艺的希腊语后缀结合，同一个后缀也组织了整族词。

latinIntro.en: The root is Greek, and no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词的词根是希腊语，没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: forms nouns of practice or study
items.meaningCN: 构成表示技艺、学科的名词

items.meaning: the person who writes or draws

definition_zh: 短语；词组；措辞；说法；乐句；用言语表达
definition_en: a small group of words that works as a unit, the particular way something is worded, a short passage in music, or to express something in words
core_image: 几块写着一个词的小木牌被细线串成一串，挂在说话人的嘴前
scene: 老师在黑板上写下一句话，用粉笔把其中三个词圈在一起，说这一小串不能拆开单独理解。She underlined the phrase twice before moving to the next line.
sceneCN: 这里 phrase 指「短语、词组」（第 1 个义项：几个词固定组合成一个单位）；句意为她把那个短语画了两遍才看下一行。图中可辨识物件：黑板、粉笔圈、串成一串的小木牌。

derivatives.zh: 由 phrase 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「短语的；由短语构成的」
由 phrase 加 -ing 构成，义为「措辞方式；乐句的处理」
由希腊语词干 phras- 加 -ology 构成，义为「措辞法；用语」
由前缀 para-（在旁边）加 phrase 构成，义为「换一种说法；改述」

senses.title: A small group of words forming a unit
senses.definition: a short group of words that acts as a single unit inside a sentence, such as a noun phrase or a verb phrase
senses.definitionCN: 在句子内部作为一个整体起作用的一小组词，如名词短语或动词短语
senses.example: The phrase in brackets can be left out.
senses.exampleCN: 括号里的那个短语可以省略。
senses.why: Greek phrasis named a manner of speaking, and this sense keeps that shape: a handful of words held together as one block of speech rather than counted one by one.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 phrasis 本指「说话的方式」，这个义项保留了那种形态：几个词被当作一整块话语握在一起，而不是逐个来数。

senses.title: A particular way of wording something
senses.definition: the words someone chooses in order to express an idea, considered as a style of expression
senses.definitionCN: 为表达某个想法而选用的词，被当作一种表达风格来看
senses.example: He turned the refusal into a polite phrase.
senses.exampleCN: 他把拒绝说成了一句客气话。
senses.why: Because a phrase is a fixed block of words, picking one block instead of another is exactly what wording means, so the noun slides from the block to the choice made among blocks.
senses.whyCN: 既然 phrase 是固定的一整块词，那么挑这一块而不挑那一块，正是「措辞」的意思，于是名词就从那一块滑到了「做选择」这件事上。

senses.title: A short passage in music
senses.definition: a short group of notes forming a unit in a melody, usually shaped so that a player or singer can breathe there
senses.definitionCN: 旋律中构成一个单位的短小音符组，通常处理成演奏者或歌者可以换气的地方
senses.example: The pianist shaped the opening phrase with great care.
senses.exampleCN: 钢琴家把开头的乐句处理得非常讲究。
senses.why: Music borrowed the term from speech: a melody is divided into breath-sized units the way a sentence is divided into word groups, so the same noun serves both arts.
senses.whyCN: 音乐从言语那里借来这个术语：旋律被分成一口气大小的单位，正如句子被分成词组，于是同一个名词同时服务于两种艺术。

senses.title: To express something in chosen words
senses.definition: to choose the words for a question, statement, or request, especially in order to control how it is received
senses.definitionCN: 为问题、陈述或请求挑选用词，尤指为了控制别人接收它的方式
senses.example: She phrased the question so that no one felt accused.
senses.exampleCN: 她把问题问得很讲究，没有人觉得是在受指责。
senses.why: English often turns a way of speaking into the act of speaking that way, so the noun for a word-block became the verb for arranging words with care.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把「一种说法」变成「按那种说法去说」的动作，于是指词块的名词就成了「仔细安排用词」的动词。

intro.en: Phrase goes back to a Greek noun for speech and style, and reached English through Latin and French as a name for a group of words.
intro.cn: phrase 可追到希腊语中表示言语与文风的名词，经拉丁语与法语进入英语，用来指一组词。

items.en: The verb phrazein meant to point out, declare, or tell, and it supplied the idea of putting a thought into speech.
items.cn: 动词 phrazein 意为指出、宣告、讲述，提供了「把想法说成话」这一观念。

items.en: The noun phrasis meant speech, manner of speaking, or style, and it named the way a thing was put into words.
items.cn: 名词 phrasis 意为言语、说话方式、文风，指一件事被说成话的方式。

items.en: Latin borrowed phrasis as a learned noun for wording and expression, and used it mainly in grammar and rhetoric.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 phrasis，作为表示措辞与表达的书卷名词，主要用于语法与修辞。

items.en: French phrase named both a group of words and a turn of speech, and English borrowed it in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 phrase 同时指一组词和一种说法，英语在十六世纪把它借了过来。

items.en: English kept the word-group sense, added the musical sense, and turned the noun into a verb for choosing words.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了「词组」义，添上音乐义，又把名词转为表示挑词造句的动词。

note.en: The look-alike group runs along the phras- stem and its derivatives; the near-meaning group gathers words for fixed expressions and for wording.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 phras- 词干及其派生词排列；近义组收表示固定表达与措辞的词。

entries.definition: Built on a phrase, especially in the term phrasal verb.
entries.definitionCN: 由短语构成，尤用于「短语动词」这一术语。

entries.definition: The way words are put together in speech or writing.
entries.definitionCN: 说话或写作中把词组织起来的方式。

entries.definition: To express someone else's meaning in different words.
entries.definitionCN: 用不同的话转述别人的意思。

entries.definition: The particular way a person or group uses words.
entries.definitionCN: 某人或某群体特有的用词方式。

entries.definition: A word or group of words used to convey an idea.
entries.definitionCN: 用来表达某个意思的词或词组。

entries.definition: A fixed group of words whose meaning cannot be guessed from the parts.
entries.definitionCN: 含义无法由各词直接推出的固定词组。

entries.definition: The words chosen for a statement, letter, or document.
entries.definitionCN: 为一段话、一封信或一份文件选用的词句。

entries.definition: A group of words with its own subject and verb, forming part of a sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 带有自己的主语和动词、构成句子一部分的一组词；分句。

normalIntro.en: The word comes from a Greek noun for speech, and its whole family keeps circling the act of putting words together.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词来自希腊语中表示言语的名词，它的整个词族都绕着「把词组织起来」这个动作转。

normal.en: Greek phrasis meant manner of speaking, so a phrase is a piece of speech cut to a size you can hold in one breath.
normal.cn: 希腊语 phrasis 意为说话方式，所以短语是被切到「一口气能拿住」那么大的一块话。

normal.en: Paraphrase adds the Greek prefix para-, beside, to phrase: the same meaning is placed beside the original in other words.
normal.cn: paraphrase 在 phrase 前加希腊语前缀 para-（在旁边）：同一个意思被用别的话放在原文旁边。

normal.en: A phrasal verb is a verb plus one or two small words, and the whole group behaves like a single verb.
normal.cn: 短语动词是一个动词加一两个小词，整组词像单个动词那样使用。

normal.en: The verb phrase means to choose the words, so a carefully phrased letter is one whose wording was reworked.
normal.cn: 动词 phrase 意为挑选用词，所以「措辞谨慎的信」就是文字被反复改过的信。

normal.en: Music uses the same noun for a short melodic unit, because a melody is breathed through in units like a sentence.
normal.cn: 音乐用同一个名词指短小的旋律单位，因为旋律也像句子一样按单位换气。

abstract.en: A phrase is a handful of words tied together, small enough to lift and large enough to carry one idea.
abstract.cn: 短语是一把被捆在一起的词，小到能拿起来，大到能装下一个意思。

abstract.en: Wording and phrased are the same insight twice: first the block of words, then the hand that arranged it.
abstract.cn: 措辞与「措辞过」是同一个洞见的两面：先是那一块词，然后是安排它的那只手。

abstract.en: When a melody is phrased well, the listener hears speech with the words taken out.
abstract.cn: 当一段旋律被处理得当时，听者听到的是抽掉了词的言语。

examples.en: The phrase in brackets can be left out.
examples.cn: 括号里的那个短语可以省略。

examples.en: He phrased the refusal so gently that nobody felt hurt.
examples.cn: 他把拒绝说得十分委婉，没有人觉得受伤。

examples.en: The opening phrase of the sonata rises like a question.
examples.cn: 奏鸣曲开头的乐句像一句问话那样升起。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗瑞兹」——说话像一串串珠子，一串就是一短语，记住 phrase。

root: 希腊语 phrazein（说出、宣告）派生 phrasis（言语、说法），经拉丁语 phrasis 与古法语 phrase 进入英语，核心是「被说成话的一组词」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a few words held together as one block; from that block come a way of wording, a musical unit, and the act of choosing words.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是几个词被握成一整块；由这一块长出措辞方式、音乐单位，以及挑词造句的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a few word tiles threaded on a string and hung in the middle of a sentence.
core.cn: 核心意象：几块写着单词的小木牌被细线串起，挂在句子中间，像一串可以整块取下的珠子。

branches.en: a chalk circle drawn around three words on a blackboard
branches.cn: 黑板上被粉笔圈住的三个词

branches.en: a letter rewritten until the refusal sounds kind
branches.cn: 一封信改到拒绝听起来也不刺人

branches.en: a melody lifting at the end of its first small unit
branches.cn: 旋律在第一个小段落末尾扬起

branches.en: a speaker pausing to choose the softer word
branches.cn: 说话人停下来挑一个更软和的词

branches.en: a sentence assembled from ready-made blocks
branches.cn: 用现成的词块拼出的一句话

intro.en: The word is carried by a Greek verb and noun for speech, a Latin borrowing, and the English endings that build its family.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示言语的希腊语动词与名词、一次拉丁语借入，以及构成其词族的英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Latin borrowed the Greek noun as phrasis, so the Latin entry is a learned loan rather than a native Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把希腊语名词借作 phrasis，所以这里列出的拉丁词是书卷借词，而非拉丁本土词根。

senses.title: Relating to the body
senses.titleCN: 身体的：跟筋骨血肉有关
senses.definition: relating to a person's or animal's body rather than the mind
senses.definitionCN: 与人或动物的身体有关，而非与心智有关
senses.example: Regular physical activity keeps the heart and lungs strong.
senses.exampleCN: 规律的身体活动能让心肺保持强健。
senses.why: Greek physis means nature, and the body is the most immediate piece of nature we own. Physical first marked what belongs to the natural, visible self.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 physis 意为“自然”，而身体是我们拥有的最直接的一块自然。physical 最早标记的就是属于这具可见的自然之身的东西。

senses.title: Relating to matter and energy
senses.titleCN: 物质的：由材料构成的那一面
senses.definition: relating to material things and their properties rather than to ideas or feelings
senses.definitionCN: 与物质事物及其属性有关，而非与观念或感受有关
senses.example: The report describes the physical properties of the new alloy.
senses.exampleCN: 报告描述了这种新合金的物理性质。
senses.why: From the body the word extends to anything that occupies space and can be measured: matter as opposed to meaning.
senses.whyCN: 从身体出发，这个词扩及一切占据空间、可被测量之物：物质，与意义相对。

senses.title: Relating to the science of physics
senses.titleCN: 物理学的：关于力、热、光、电的那门学问
senses.definition: belonging to physics, the science of matter, energy, and their interactions
senses.definitionCN: 属于物理学的，即研究物质、能量及其相互作用的科学
senses.example: Physical chemistry bridges the two departments.
senses.exampleCN: 物理化学把这两个系科连接起来。
senses.why: Physics took its name from the same Greek root. Anything studied by that science is physical in this narrower, technical sense.
senses.whyCN: 物理学（physics）的名字来自同一个希腊词根。被这门科学研究的东西，就在这个更窄的专业意义上属于 physical。

senses.title: Real and tangible
senses.titleCN: 有形的：真实存在、摸得着
senses.definition: existing in a real, material form that can be touched, seen, or measured
senses.definitionCN: 以真实的、物质的形态存在，可以被触摸、看见或测量
senses.example: The plan finally took physical form as a printed book.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划最终以一本印刷书的实体形态出现。
senses.why: If matter is what can be measured, then 'physical' becomes a guarantee of reality: not imagined, not merely promised.
senses.whyCN: 如果物质就是可被测量的东西，那么 physical 就成了“真实”的保证：不是想象，不只是承诺。

senses.title: Involving bodily force or contact
senses.titleCN: 动身体的：靠力气、会碰撞
senses.definition: involving bodily effort, contact, or force, as in sport or in violence
senses.definitionCN: 涉及身体用力、接触或强制，如体育或暴力场合
senses.example: Ice hockey is a far more physical game than badminton.
senses.exampleCN: 冰球比羽毛球激烈得多，身体对抗也多得多。
senses.why: Bodies in contact is the most visible kind of physical interaction, so the word comes to describe rough, hands-on activity.
senses.whyCN: 身体相互接触是最显眼的物理性互动，所以这个词被用来形容粗重的、动手动脚的活动。

senses.title: Belonging to the natural world
senses.titleCN: 自然的：山川气候，非人造
senses.definition: belonging to nature, especially in contrast with what humans build or arrange
senses.definitionCN: 属于自然界的，尤与人为建造或安排的事物相对
senses.example: Physical geography studies rivers, mountains, and climate.
senses.exampleCN: 自然地理学研究河流、山脉与气候。
senses.why: Physis is nature itself. This sense keeps the oldest meaning most faithfully: whatever is not made by us.
senses.whyCN: physis 就是“自然”。这个义项最忠实地保留了最古老的含义：非由我们制造的一切。

senses.title: Noun: a medical check-up
senses.definition: a medical examination of the body, usually called a physical or a physical exam
senses.definitionCN: 对身体进行的医学检查，通常说 a physical 或 a physical exam
senses.example: She has her annual physical every September.
senses.exampleCN: 她每年九月做一次年度体检。
senses.why: The noun is short for physical examination. The adjective turned into a name for the event in which the body is examined.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词是 physical examination 的省略。形容词变成了那场“检查身体”的事件之名。

senses.title: Legal: material evidence
senses.definition: in law, referring to objects and traces that can be examined, as opposed to testimony
senses.definitionCN: 法律上指可被检验的实物与痕迹，与证言相对
senses.example: Physical evidence placed him at the scene.
senses.exampleCN: 实物证据表明他曾在现场。
senses.why: Courts separate what can be held and tested from what is only said. Physical marks the first category.
senses.whyCN: 法庭把可以拿在手里检验的东西与只是被说出来的话分开。physical 标记的是前一类。

intro.en: Physical descends from the Greek word for nature. Its story is the story of physis: first what grows, then the whole natural order, then the body, then matter itself.
intro.cn: physical 源自希腊语中表示“自然”的那个词。它的历史就是 physis 的历史：先指生长之物，再指整个自然秩序，再指身体，最后指物质本身。

items.en: Phyein meant 'to grow, to bring forth'. It comes from PIE *bheu- 'to grow, to be', the root behind English be and build.
items.cn: phyein 意为“生长、生出”。它来自原始印欧语 *bheu-“生长、存在”，英语 be 与 build 也出自这条根。

items.en: Physis meant 'nature' but literally 'growth'. To the Greeks, a thing's nature was what it grew into when nothing interfered.
items.cn: physis 意为“自然”，字面却是“生长”。在希腊人看来，一物的自然就是它在不受干扰时会长成的样子。

items.en: Physikos meant 'natural, of nature', and also 'about natural things'. It described both the subject matter and the person who studied it.
items.cn: physikos 意为“自然的、属于自然的”，也指“研究自然之物的”。它既描述研究对象，也描述研究的人。

items.en: Latin physicus meant 'natural' and, in later use, 'a physician'. Medieval physica covered medicine and natural philosophy together.
items.cn: 拉丁语 physicus 意为“自然的”，后期也指“医生”。中世纪的 physica 把医学与自然哲学合在一起。

items.en: English physical appears in the 16th century with the sense 'of nature'. The sense 'of the body' follows within the same century, and the sense tied to the science of physics develops later.
items.cn: 英语 physical 出现于 16 世纪，意为“自然的”。“身体的”这一义在同一个世纪内跟进；与物理学这门科学相关的义项则更晚发展出来。

items.en: The modern word splits into the body (physical training), matter (physical properties), science (physical chemistry), and reality (physical evidence), all resting on the same Greek idea of nature.
items.cn: 现代这个词分向身体（physical training）、物质（physical properties）、科学（physical chemistry）与实在（physical evidence），全都依托同一个希腊的“自然”观念。

note.en: The first group shares the Greek root for nature. The second group collects words for what is bodily or materially real.
note.cn: 第一组共享表示“自然”的希腊词根。第二组收表示“身体的”或“物质上真实”的词。

entries.definition: the science of matter and energy. Greek physika meant natural things; the plural became the name of the science.
entries.definitionCN: 研究物质与能量的科学。希腊语 physika 意为“自然之物”，其复数形式成了这门学科的名字。

entries.definition: the shape and build of a body. It comes through French from Latin physicus, keeping the bodily focus.
entries.definitionCN: 身体的形状与结构。它经法语来自拉丁语 physicus，保留了“身体”这一重心。

entries.definition: a doctor of medicine. In medieval Latin physicus meant a healer of natural things, that is, the body.
entries.definitionCN: 医生。在中世纪拉丁语里，physicus 指治疗自然之物（即身体）的人。

entries.definition: the study of what lies beyond the physical. Meta- 'after, beyond' plus physics: the books that came after the physics books.
entries.definitionCN: 研究物理世界之外的东西的学问。meta-“之后、超越”加 physics：排在物理学著作之后的那批书。

entries.definition: relating to the body. Bodily overlaps physical in sense 01 but has no material or scientific senses.
entries.definitionCN: 与身体有关的。bodily 在第 1 义项上与 physical 重叠，但没有物质义或科学义。

entries.definition: made of matter, or concerned with possessions. Material fits sense 02; physical also covers the body and physics.
entries.definitionCN: 由物质构成的，或与财物有关的。material 对应第 2 义项；physical 还覆盖身体与物理学。

entries.definition: having a body. Corporeal is the formal word for sense 01 and is rarely used of objects.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有肉身的。corporeal 是第 1 义项的正式说法，很少用于物体。

entries.definition: able to be touched or clearly perceived. Tangible matches sense 04 and stresses the sense of touch.
entries.definitionCN: 能被触摸或清楚感知的。tangible 对应第 4 义项，强调触觉。

entries.definition: existing in nature, not made by people. Natural matches sense 06 and shares the same underlying idea of physis.
entries.definitionCN: 存在于自然界、非人造的。natural 对应第 6 义项，底层同样是 physis 的观念。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the body that can be touched, the material object, the physics lab, the printed book, and the sports field.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：摸得到的身体、物质对象、物理实验室、印成书的实体、运动场上的对抗。

normal.en: Physical = what you can poke. If your finger stops at it, it is physical.
normal.cn: physical＝你能戳到的东西。手指停在上面的，就是 physical。

normal.en: Physis is nature, and your body is the piece of nature you carry around.
normal.cn: physis 是自然，而你的身体就是你随身携带的那块自然。

normal.en: Physics and physical are the same root: one is the science, the other is what the science studies.
normal.cn: physics 与 physical 同根：一个是学科，一个是这门学科研究的东西。

normal.en: A physical exam is literally a body check: the adjective became the name of the appointment.
normal.cn: a physical exam 字面就是“对身体做的检查”：形容词变成了那次预约的名字。

normal.en: Metaphysics sits after physics: meta- means after, so it is the study of what the physical cannot cover.
normal.cn: metaphysics 排在 physics 之后：meta- 意为“之后”，所以它研究 physical 覆盖不到的部分。

abstract.en: The physical is the layer that resists you; everything else is negotiation.
abstract.cn: 物理层就是会抵抗你的那一层；其余的一切都是协商。

abstract.en: Nature, body, matter, reality: one Greek word supplied four different borders for what counts as real.
abstract.cn: 自然、身体、物质、实在：一个希腊词为“什么算真实”划出了四道不同的边界。

abstract.en: To call something physical is to claim it can be measured; measurement is the modern form of the old word for nature.
abstract.cn: 说某物是 physical，就是声称它可以被测量；测量是那个古老的“自然”一词的现代形态。

examples.en: After the accident he needed months of physical therapy before he could walk unaided.
examples.cn: 事故之后他需要数月的物理治疗，才能独立行走。

examples.en: The two servers are physically separate even though they share one logical name.
examples.cn: 这两台服务器虽然共用一个逻辑名称，物理上是分开的。

examples.en: Detectives found physical evidence that contradicted the witness's account.
examples.cn: 警探找到了与证人陈述相矛盾的实物证据。

dict_mnemonic.text: “菲兹克”听起来像“非此刻”——不是此刻的想法，而是此刻摸得着的东西：physical 物质的、身体的

root: 希腊语 phyein“生长”→ physis“自然（生长之物）”→ physikos“自然的”→ 拉丁 physicus → 英语 physical；与 physics、physique、physician、metaphysics 同根。

sensesIntro.en: Everything here comes from one Greek word for nature. The body is nature closest to us; matter is nature outside us; physics is nature studied; a physical exam is the body inspected; physical evidence is reality that can be handled.
sensesIntro.cn: 这里的一切都出自一个表示“自然”的希腊词。身体是离我们最近的自然；物质是我们之外的自然；物理学是被研究的自然；体检是被检查的身体；实物证据是可以拿在手里的实在。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressing against a solid surface and feeling it push back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按在坚实表面上，感到它顶回来。

branches.en: BODY: the natural self and the examination of it.
branches.cn: 身体：自然的自身，以及对它的检查。

branches.en: MATTER: material properties, tangible reality, and evidence that can be handled.
branches.cn: 物质：物质属性、可触摸的实在、可拿在手里的证据。

branches.en: SCIENCE: the department that studies matter and energy.
branches.cn: 科学：研究物质与能量的那门学科。

branches.en: FORCE: bodies in contact, effort and collision.
branches.cn: 力：身体相触，用力与碰撞。

branches.en: NATURE: the non-human world, kept closest to the Greek original.
branches.cn: 自然：非人造的世界，最贴近希腊原义。

intro.en: The family rests on the Greek noun for nature and its adjective. English adds the usual endings for sciences, persons, and properties.
intro.cn: 这个词族建立在希腊语表示“自然”的名词及其形容词上。英语加上表示学科、人物与性质的常见词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin borrowed physicus and physica, and through them the root reached medicine before it reached physics.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语借入 physicus 与 physica，这条词根先进入医学，后才进入物理学。

items.meaningCN: 表示研究者或从业者的后缀

definition_zh: 身体上；体力上；体格上；物质上；按物理规律地；实际地；亲自地；在物理空间中地；有形地
definition_en: in a way that concerns the body, the material world, or the laws of physics, or in person rather than in thought or at a distance
core_image: 身体撞到墙时的那一声闷响，和随之而来的一阵疼
scene: 医生说这项检查要看他的体力，而不只是看化验单。The test asks whether he is physically able to lift those boxes.
sceneCN: 这里 physically 是「体力上」（第 2 个义项：就身体的力量与能力而言）；句意：这项检查要确认他在体力上能不能搬动那些箱子；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 身体上；体力上；物质上；按物理规律地；亲自地

senses.title: In the body
senses.definition: in a way that involves or affects the body, as opposed to the mind or the emotions
senses.definitionCN: 以涉及或影响身体的方式，相对于心智或情感
senses.example: After the crash he was shaken but not physically hurt.
senses.exampleCN: 撞车之后他受了惊，但身体没有受伤。
senses.why: Greek physis is 'nature', the growing body. Physical first meant 'natural' and then 'bodily'; physically marks the place where the wall is met by flesh rather than by thought.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 physis 是“自然”，即生长着的身体。physical 先表示“自然的”，再表示“身体的”；physically 标记的是墙被肉而不是被思想撞到的那个地方。

senses.title: In terms of bodily strength
senses.definition: with regard to a person's strength, stamina, or ability to do bodily work
senses.definitionCN: 就一个人的力量、耐力或从事体力工作的能力而言
senses.example: The job is physically demanding but not technically hard.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工作对体力要求高，技术上却不难。
senses.why: The body is also a tool with a capacity. This sense measures that capacity, which is why a task can be physically hard while being mentally easy.
senses.whyCN: 身体也是一件有容量的工具。这个义项测量这种容量，所以一项任务可以体力上很难、脑力上却很简单。

senses.title: In build or appearance
senses.definition: with regard to the shape, size, or visible condition of a person's body
senses.definitionCN: 就一个人身体的形状、大小或可见状态而言
senses.example: He looked physically stronger than he had in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 他看起来比春天时体格更强壮。
senses.why: The wall's sound tells you something about the body that hit it. Here physically describes the body as an object others can see and measure.
senses.whyCN: 撞墙的声音能说明撞上去的身体是什么样。这里的 physically 把身体描述成他人能看见、能测量的对象。

senses.title: In the material world
senses.definition: in a material or tangible way, as opposed to symbolically, legally, or in thought
senses.definitionCN: 以物质的、可触摸的方式，相对于象征、法律或思想层面
senses.example: The two offices are physically separate but share one budget.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个办公室在物理空间上是分开的，却共用一份预算。
senses.why: From the body the word widens to matter in general. Anything that occupies space and can be bumped into counts as physically real, even if it is not alive.
senses.whyCN: 从身体开始，这个词扩展到一般物质。任何占据空间、能被撞到的东西都算物理上真实，即使它不是活的。

senses.title: According to the laws of physics
senses.definition: in a way that obeys, or is explained by, physical laws such as conservation of energy or causality
senses.definitionCN: 以遵守或被物理规律（如能量守恒或因果性）解释的方式
senses.example: A perpetual motion machine is physically impossible.
senses.exampleCN: 永动机在物理上是不可能的。
senses.why: Here the word invokes the discipline, not the body. Physically impossible means the wall cannot be walked through, no matter how strong the will.
senses.whyCN: 这里调用的是学科，而不是身体。physically impossible 意味着无论意志多强，墙都穿不过去。

senses.title: Actually, not merely on paper
senses.titleCN: 实际存在而非纸面上的
senses.definition: in actual fact, so that something exists or happens rather than being only planned or claimed
senses.definitionCN: 在事实上，使某物真实存在或发生，而不只是被计划或被声称
senses.example: The backup site exists physically, not only in the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 备份站点是实际存在的，不只存在于计划里。
senses.why: A plan is weightless. Physically real means the thing can be visited, weighed, or unplugged, which is the test the word applies to claims.
senses.whyCN: 计划没有重量。physically real 意味着这东西可以被走访、称重或拔掉电源，这就是这个词对声明所用的检验。

senses.title: In person, not remotely
senses.definition: by being present in the same place, rather than by phone, letter, or network
senses.definitionCN: 通过身处同一地点，而不是通过电话、信件或网络
senses.example: The witness must appear physically before the court.
senses.exampleCN: 证人必须亲自出庭。
senses.why: A voice on a wire has no body. Physically present restores the wall and the room: the person can be seen, touched, and held to account in one place.
senses.whyCN: 电线里的声音没有身体。physically present 把墙和房间还回来：人能被看见、被触到，并在同一个地方被追究。

senses.title: At a point in space
senses.definition: in a particular location in space, as opposed to being distributed, virtual, or undefined
senses.definitionCN: 位于空间中的某个特定位置，相对于分散、虚拟或位置不明
senses.example: The servers are physically in Frankfurt but logically in the cloud.
senses.exampleCN: 这些服务器物理上位于法兰克福，逻辑上却在“云”里。
senses.why: The word insists on coordinates. A cloud has no address until someone points to a building, and physically is the adverb that points.
senses.whyCN: 这个词坚持要坐标。云没有地址，直到有人指向一栋楼，而 physically 就是那只指过去的手。

senses.title: In a tangible form
senses.definition: in a form that can be touched or handled, such as a printed copy or a physical object
senses.definitionCN: 以能够触摸或拿取的形式，如印刷副本或实物
senses.example: The archive keeps the files physically as well as digitally.
senses.exampleCN: 档案馆既保存数字文件，也保存实体文件。
senses.why: A file can be a ghost in a machine. Physically kept means there is paper you can drop, which is the oldest test of whether something is really there.
senses.whyCN: 文件可以是机器里的幽灵。以物理形态保存下来，意味着有可以掉在地上的纸，这是检验某物是否真的存在的最古老办法。

intro.en: Physically is physical plus -ly. Physical comes from Latin physicus 'natural, of nature', from Greek physikos, from physis 'nature'. Physis derives from phyein 'to bring forth, grow', so the oldest sense is not 'body' but 'what grows by itself'. English first used physical for medicine and natural things, then for the body, and only later for the science of physics.
intro.cn: physically 是 physical 加 -ly。physical 来自拉丁 physicus“自然的、属于自然的”，出自希腊 physikos，再上溯 physis“自然”。physis 又出自 phyein“产生、生长”，所以最古老的意义不是“身体”，而是“自己长出来的东西”。英语最早用 physical 指医药与自然事物，之后指身体，再往后才指物理学。

items.en: Physis means 'nature, natural form, growth'. The verb phyein means 'to bring forth, grow'. The physical is therefore first of all the growing world, not the body as opposed to the mind.
items.cn: physis 意为“自然、自然形态、生长”。动词 phyein 意为“产生、生长”。所以 physical 首先是生长着的世界，而不是与心智相对的身体。

items.en: Physicus in Latin means 'natural, of nature', and also 'a natural philosopher'. English physical enters in the 14th century with the sense 'medicinal, healing', since medicine studied natural bodies.
items.cn: 拉丁 physicus 意为“自然的、属于自然的”，也指“自然哲学家”。英语 physical 在 14 世纪进入，义为“医药的、治疗性的”，因为医学研究的是自然身体。

items.en: The sense 'bodily, of the body' becomes common, and the noun physics settles as the name of the science of matter and motion.
items.cn: “身体的、肉体的”这一义项在 16 世纪变得常见，名词 physics 则固定为研究物质与运动的科学名称。

items.en: Physically extends from the body to matter in general and to the laws of nature: physically impossible, physically separate.
items.cn: physically 从身体扩展到一般物质与自然规律：物理上不可能、物理上分开。

items.en: The adverb is the plain -ly form of physical. No new meaning is added: it turns 'of the body or of matter' into 'in the body or in matter'.
items.cn: 副词是 physical 的规则 -ly 形式。没有增加新意义：它把“身体或物质的”变成“在身体上或在物质中”。

items.en: Fiscal looks close but comes from Latin fiscus 'basket, treasury', so it means 'of public money'. Physique shares the physis root but names the shape of the body. Physician also shares physis, since medicine was the study of nature.
items.cn: fiscal 看起来相近，却来自拉丁 fiscus“篮子、国库”，所以意为“财政的”。physique 共享 physis 词根，却指身体的形状。physician 也共享 physis，因为医学本是对自然的研究。

note.en: The first group separates the physis family from the fiscal trap. The second group compares bodily, materially, tangibly, and actually, the four adverbs closest to physically.
note.cn: 第一组把 physis 词族与 fiscal 陷阱分开。第二组比较 bodily、materially、tangibly、actually，这四个副词最接近 physically。

entries.definition: relating to the body, to matter, or to physics. The adverb only turns this into a manner.
entries.definitionCN: 与身体、物质或物理学有关的。副词只是把它变成一种方式。

entries.definition: the shape and build of a person's body. It is a noun, so it names the body's form rather than a way of acting.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人身体的形状与体格。它是名词，命名身体形态而非行为方式。

entries.definition: a doctor of medicine. It shares physis because medicine was once the study of natural bodies.
entries.definitionCN: 医生。它共享 physis，因为医学曾是对自然身体的研究。

entries.definition: relating to public money, taxes, and budgets. Its root is fiscus 'basket, treasury', so it has no bodily or physical sense.
entries.definitionCN: 与公共资金、税收和预算有关的。它的词根是 fiscus“篮子、国库”，所以没有身体或物理含义。

entries.definition: relating to the body, especially as opposed to the mind. It is narrower than physically, which also covers matter and physics.
entries.definitionCN: 与身体有关的，尤指相对于心智。它比 physically 窄，后者也覆盖物质与物理学。

entries.definition: in a way that concerns matter or material wealth. Its 'physical' sense is about stuff; its other sense is about money.
entries.definitionCN: 在涉及物质或物质财富的方式上。它的“物理”义关乎东西，另一义则关乎金钱。

entries.definition: in a way that can be touched or clearly perceived. It is the touchable side of physically, not the legal or logical one.
entries.definitionCN: 以可触摸或清楚感知的方式。它是 physically 可触摸的一面，而不是法律或逻辑的一面。

entries.definition: in fact, really. It contrasts with what is said or expected, while physically contrasts with what is mental or virtual.
entries.definitionCN: 事实上、真的。它与所言或所期待相对，而 physically 与心智或虚拟相对。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: physis 'nature', phyein 'grow', Latin physicus, the 14th-century medicinal sense, and the fiscus trap.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：physis“自然”、phyein“生长”、拉丁 physicus、14 世纪的医药义，以及 fiscus 陷阱。

normal.en: Physis is 'nature, growth': physical first meant 'natural', and only later 'bodily'.
normal.cn: physis 是“自然、生长”：physical 先表示“自然的”，后来才表示“身体的”。

normal.en: The adverb is just -ly: physically means 'in the body or in matter', the same relation with a different position.
normal.cn: 副词只是 -ly：physically 意为“在身体上或在物质中”，关系相同，位置不同。

normal.en: Medicine gave the word its early home, which is why physician and physical share a root.
normal.cn: 医学给了这个词早期归宿，所以 physician 与 physical 共享词根。

normal.en: A plan has no weight; physically real means you can go there and put your hand on it.
normal.cn: 计划没有重量；physically real 意味着你能走过去把手放上去。

normal.en: Fiscal looks like a cousin but comes from fiscus 'treasury'; money is not matter.
normal.cn: fiscal 看起来像表亲，却出自 fiscus“国库”；钱不是物质。

abstract.en: The sound of a body hitting a wall is the oldest proof that there is a wall.
abstract.cn: 身体撞上墙的声音，是“墙确实存在”最古老的证据。

abstract.en: A voice on a wire can lie about where it is; a body in a chair cannot.
abstract.cn: 电线里的声音可以谎报自己在哪；椅子上的身体不行。

abstract.en: A cloud is a place until someone asks where its buildings are.
abstract.cn: 云是一个地方，直到有人问它的楼在哪里。

examples.en: The tablet is physically identical to the one sold last year.
examples.cn: 这台平板与去年出售的那台在物理上完全相同。

examples.en: She was physically exhausted after the climb.
examples.cn: 爬完之后她身体极度疲惫。

examples.en: The director was physically present at the signing.
examples.cn: 签署时董事亲自到场。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「菲兹克利」——身体“菲”常实在地撞到墙上，发出一声“兹”，疼是真的 → physically 身体上；物质上；物理上（只借音，不表词源）

root: 拉丁 physicus「自然的」，出自希腊 physikos 与 physis「自然」，再上溯 phyein「产生、生长」；后缀 -ly 构成副词。核心是「身体撞到墙时那声闷响，以及随之而来的疼」。同族含 physical、physics、physique、physician；fiscal（fiscus「国库」）只是形近，词根不同。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of physically all begin with a body meeting the world. What changes is the aspect in view: the flesh, the strength, the build, matter in general, the laws of nature, actual existence, presence in person, location in space, or a tangible copy.
sensesIntro.cn: physically 的九个义项都从“身体与世界相遇”开始。变化的是所看的侧面：肉、力量、体格、一般物质、自然规律、实际存在、亲自到场、空间位置，还是一份有形的副本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the dull sound of a body hitting a wall, and the pain that proves the wall is there.
core.cn: 核心意象：身体撞到墙时的那声闷响，以及证明墙确实存在的那阵疼。

branches.en: THE BODY: flesh that can be hurt, strength that can be spent, and a build that can be seen.
branches.cn: 身体：会被伤到的肉、会被消耗的力量，以及看得见的体格。

branches.en: MATTER AND FORM: the material world at large, and objects that can be touched or printed.
branches.cn: 物质与形式：广义的物质世界，以及可触摸或可印刷的实物。

branches.en: THE LAWS: what physics permits or forbids, regardless of desire.
branches.cn: 规律：物理学允许或禁止什么，与愿望无关。

branches.en: REAL AND LOCATED: actual existence rather than plans, and a point with real coordinates.
branches.cn: 真实且有位置：实际存在而非计划，以及有真实坐标的地点。

branches.en: PRESENT IN PERSON: a body in the room rather than a voice on a wire.
branches.cn: 亲自到场：房间里的身体，而不是电线里的声音。

intro.en: Physically is physical + -ly. Physical is Latin physicus, from Greek physikos and physis 'nature'. The family is unusual because it produced three separate English words from one root: physical, physics, and physician.
intro.cn: physically 是 physical 加 -ly。physical 是拉丁 physicus，出自希腊 physikos 与 physis“自然”。这个词族不寻常之处在于，同一个词根产生了三个各自独立的英语词：physical、physics、physician。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is physicus 'natural, of nature', also used as a noun for a natural philosopher, and physica 'natural things, natural science'. Greek supplied physis and physikos.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 physicus“自然的、属于自然的”，也作名词指自然哲学家，以及 physica“自然事物、自然科学”。希腊语提供了 physis 与 physikos。

items.meaning: in the body, in matter, or according to physics
items.meaningCN: 在身体上、在物质中，或按物理规律（-ly 副词）
items.example: The two buildings are physically joined.
items.exampleCN: 这两栋楼在物理上是相连的。

items.meaning: of the body, of matter, or of physics
items.meaningCN: 身体的、物质的或物理学的
items.example: Physical evidence was collected at the site.
items.exampleCN: 现场收集到了实物证据。

items.structure: Greek ta physika 'natural things', via Latin physica
items.meaning: the science of matter, energy, and motion
items.meaningCN: 研究物质、能量与运动的科学；物理学
items.example: Physics explains why the bridge holds.
items.exampleCN: 物理学解释了这座桥为什么撑得住。

items.meaning: the build and shape of a body

items.structure: Old French fisicien, from Latin physicus
items.example: The physician ordered a chest X-ray.
items.exampleCN: 医生要求做胸部 X 光检查。

items.meaning: the quality of being bodily or tangible
items.example: The dance stresses weight and physicality.
items.exampleCN: 这段舞蹈强调重量与身体感。

items.meaning: treatment by movement and physical means
items.meaningCN: 用运动与物理手段进行的治疗；物理疗法
items.exampleCN: 物理治疗让他的肩膀恢复了。

items.meaningCN: 与公共资金有关的；财政的（fiscus 国库）
items.example: The fiscal year ends in March.

items.structure: Old French fisique < Latin physica < Greek physike 'natural science, medicine'
items.meaning: medicine or the art of healing (archaic); to treat with medicine
items.meaningCN: 药；医术（古旧用法）；用药物治疗
items.example: The old herbals list a physic for fever.
items.exampleCN: 古旧的草药书里列有一种退烧的药。

latinEntries.structure: Latin adjective and noun, from Greek physikos
latinEntries.meaning: natural, of nature; a natural philosopher
latinEntries.meaningCN: 自然的、属于自然的；自然哲学家
篮子、国库（与 physis 无关）
