definition_zh: 医生；内科医生；机构医官；医治者
definition_en: a doctor of medicine, especially one who treats illness with drugs and advice rather than surgery; also a doctor attached to an institution, or a person or thing that heals
core_image: 一位白衣医生先把听诊器捂热，才贴到病人胸口
scene: 诊室的窗半开着，医生把听诊器在掌心捂了一会儿，才贴到老人胸口。The physician asked a few quiet questions before writing the prescription.
sceneCN: 这里 physician 指「医生」（第 1 个义项：正式称呼的医学从业者）；句意为这位医生先轻声问了几个问题，才写下处方。图中可辨识物件：听诊器、处方笺、半开的窗。

pos.zh: 医生；内科医生；机构医官；医治者

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语 physis（自然）加 -al 构成，义为「身体的；物质的」
由同一词干加 -ics 构成，义为「物理学」
由 physics 加 -ist 构成，义为「物理学家」
经法语借入，指「体格；体形」

senses.title: A doctor of medicine, used as a formal title
senses.definition: a person who is qualified and licensed to practise medicine, especially when the word is used as a formal or respectful title
senses.definitionCN: 有资格并获准行医的人，尤用作正式或尊敬的称呼
senses.example: The physician listened to her breathing for a full minute.
senses.exampleCN: 这位医生听她的呼吸听了整整一分钟。
senses.why: Greek physis meant nature, and medicine was once studied as part of natural knowledge, so the healer was named after the natural world he read.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 physis 意为自然，医学当年被当作自然之学的一部分来研究，于是治病的人就按他所解读的自然界来命名。

senses.title: A doctor who treats disease without operating
senses.definition: a doctor who works mainly through drugs, diet, and advice rather than by cutting into the body
senses.definitionCN: 主要通过药物、饮食与建议治病，而不是切开身体的医生
senses.example: The surgeon sent the patient back to the physician for drug treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生把病人送回内科医生那里接受药物治疗。
senses.why: English long used physic for medicine as a body of knowledge, so a physician was the one who worked through medicine, while a surgeon worked with hands and steel; the two roles split along that line.
senses.whyCN: 英语长期用 physic 指作为一门知识体系的医学，所以 physician 是靠药物医理工作的人，而外科医生靠双手与刀剪，两种角色就沿这条线分开。

senses.title: The doctor appointed to an institution
senses.definition: the doctor officially attached to a school, prison, army unit, or ship, and known by that post
senses.definitionCN: 正式受聘于学校、监狱、部队或船只的医生，以其职位为人所知
senses.example: The camp physician signed the health certificate.
senses.exampleCN: 营地的医官在健康证明上签了字。
senses.why: Since the word is a title, an institution uses it for the doctor it appoints, and the sense settles on the post rather than on the individual's skill.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词本身是头衔，机构就用它来指自己聘任的那位医生，义项便落在「职位」上，而不强调个人医术高低。

senses.title: A healer of hurts that are not bodily
senses.definition: a person or thing imagined as curing a hurt of the mind or of society rather than of the body
senses.definitionCN: 被想象成能治好心灵或社会创伤的人或事物，而非医治身体
senses.example: Time is the physician of wounds that words cannot reach.
senses.exampleCN: 时间是言语够不到的伤口的医生。
senses.why: Once the word names the healer of the body, it can be carried over to whatever repairs damage, because the picture of the cure travels more easily than the body it first described.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既然指身体的医治者，就能被搬到任何修补损伤的事物上，因为「治愈」这个图像比它最初描述的身体更容易被搬走。

intro.en: Physician comes from the Greek word for nature by way of the Latin and French names for natural science, because medicine was once taught as part of that science.
intro.cn: physician 经由拉丁语与法语中「自然之学」的名称，上溯到希腊语表示自然的词，因为医学当年是作为这门学问的一部分来教的。

items.en: Physis meant nature, and ta physika meant natural things or natural science, including the study of the body.
items.cn: physis 意为自然，ta physika 指自然之物或自然之学，其中也包括对身体的研究。

items.en: The adjective physikos meant natural, and the noun physike named natural philosophy, the broad study that contained medicine.
items.cn: 形容词 physikos 意为「自然的」，名词 physike 指自然哲学，这门宽泛的学问包含医术。

items.en: Latin physica borrowed the Greek noun for natural science, and medieval writers used it for medicine as the healing branch of that science.
items.cn: 拉丁语 physica 借入这个表示自然之学的希腊名词，中世纪的作者用它指其中治病的那一支，即医学。

items.en: Old French fisique meant both natural science and medicine, and fisicien named the person who practised it.
items.cn: 古法语 fisique 兼指自然之学与医学，fisicien 则指从事这一行的人。

items.en: Middle English took the French word as physicion and later spelled it physician; physics went on to mean natural science while physician kept the medical sense.
items.cn: 中古英语把法语词写作 physicion，后来定型为 physician；physics 继续指自然科学，而 physician 保住了医学义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms on the Greek stem for nature and states the discipline each one belongs to; the near-meaning group gathers words for people who treat the sick.
note.cn: 形近组收同一个希腊语「自然」词干上的形式，并点明各自所属学科；近义组收表示治病之人的词。

entries.definition: A scientist who studies matter, energy, and forces; it shares the Greek root with physician but names a different discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 研究物质、能量与力的科学家；与 physician 同出希腊语词根，但学科不同。

entries.definition: The science of matter, energy, and motion.
entries.definitionCN: 研究物质、能量与运动的科学；物理学。

entries.definition: An old word for medicine, and the base from which the healers title was formed.
entries.definitionCN: 医学的古称，也是「医生」这一头衔的构词基础。

entries.definition: Relating to the body or to material things rather than to the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 与身体或物质事物有关，而非与心智有关。

entries.definition: A person qualified to treat the sick, used as a general title.
entries.definitionCN: 有资格治病的人，用作一般称呼。

entries.definition: A doctor, or a medical student or worker.
entries.definitionCN: 医生，或医学生、医务工作者。

entries.definition: A doctor who performs operations inside the body.
entries.definitionCN: 在身体上动手术的医生；外科医生。

entries.definition: A community doctor who treats ordinary illnesses and refers patients onward.
entries.definitionCN: 在社区看常见病并负责转诊的医生；全科医生。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on the Greek noun for nature, because medicine was once a branch of natural knowledge.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在希腊语表示自然的名词上，因为医学曾是自然之学的一个分支。

normal.en: Physician rests on Greek physis, nature, the same stem that gives physics and physical.
normal.cn: physician 立在希腊语 physis（自然）上，与 physics、physical 同用一个词干。

normal.en: The Old French form fisicien meant one who practises physic, and physic was the old English name for medicine.
normal.cn: 古法语形式 fisicien 指「行医的人」，而 physic 是英语里医学的旧称。

normal.en: Physicist and physician look like twins because both grew from physis, but one studies forces and the other treats patients.
normal.cn: physicist 与 physician 看着像双胞胎，因为都从 physis 长出，但一个研究力，一个治病人。

normal.en: Surgeon comes from a different root, which is why hospitals keep the two titles apart on their signs.
normal.cn: surgeon 来自另一个词根，所以医院的牌子上要把这两个头衔分开写。

normal.en: The plural is physicians, and the word is formal: a clinic writes physician where a friend would simply say doctor.
normal.cn: 复数是 physicians；这个词较正式：诊所写 physician 的地方，朋友之间只会说 doctor。

abstract.en: Nature sits inside the name of the healer: the first physicians read the body as part of the natural world.
abstract.cn: 自然藏在医治者的名字里：最早的医生把身体当作自然界的一部分来读。

abstract.en: One ancient word for nature split into two modern jobs, one reading matter and one reading symptoms.
abstract.cn: 一个古老的「自然」之词分成了两份现代职业，一份读物质，一份读症状。

abstract.en: A title of three syllables keeps a distance that the short word doctor does not.
abstract.cn: 三个音节的头衔保持了一种距离，短词 doctor 就没有这种距离。

examples.en: The physician asked a few quiet questions before writing the prescription.
examples.cn: 这位医生轻声问了几个问题，才写下处方。

examples.en: Her family physician has known her since she was a child.
examples.cn: 她的家庭医生从她小时候就认识她。

examples.en: The camp physician signed the health certificate.
examples.cn: 营地的医官在健康证明上签了字。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费心诊」——医生为病人费心诊断，physician 就是医生。

root: 希腊语 physis（自然）→ physike（自然之学，含医学）→ 拉丁语 physica → 古法语 fisique 与 fisicien → 中古英语 physicion → physician；与 physicist 同源而异科。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a healer named after nature; from that identity come the formal title, the doctor who works without a knife, the appointed post, and the healing figure in metaphor.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「以自然之理治病的人」；由这一身份分出正式头衔、不动刀的内科医生、受聘的职位，以及比喻里的医治者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a doctor warming a stethoscope in one hand before pressing it to a patient's chest.
core.cn: 核心意象：一位医生先把听诊器在掌心捂热，再贴到病人胸口。

branches.en: a doctor's office with a prescription pad open on the desk
branches.cn: 诊室里摊开着处方笺

branches.en: a physician reading test results instead of holding a scalpel
branches.cn: 内科医生看化验单而不是握手术刀

branches.en: a school doctor signing a pupil's form
branches.cn: 校医在学生表格上签字

branches.en: an old book described as a cure for a tired mind
branches.cn: 一本被说成能治心累的旧书

branches.en: a hospital corridor with medicine on one door and surgery on the other
branches.cn: 医院走廊上一扇门写内科，一扇门写外科

intro.en: A Greek noun for nature, its adjective, the Latin and French forms of natural science, and two English endings carry the word.
intro.cn: 希腊语表示自然的名词、它的形容词、自然之学的拉丁与法语形式，以及两个英语词尾共同支撑这个词。

latinIntro.en: Latin took the Greek adjective and noun as physicus and physica, and these forms stand behind the French word for medicine.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把希腊语的形容词与名词接收为 physicus 与 physica，这两个形式正是法语中「医学」一词背后的来源。

definition_zh: 物理学家；物理学研究者
definition_en: a person who studies or is trained in physics, either as a researcher or as a teacher
core_image: 一位研究者站在写满公式的黑板前，手里握着粉笔，桌上摆着被拆开的旧钟表与一块磁铁
scene: 研究所的走廊里，一位研究者正把新的测量结果贴到公告板上，同行围过来争论误差来源。A researcher pinned a new set of measurements to the board in the corridor, and colleagues gathered to argue about the source of error that the physicist had reported.
sceneCN: 这里指「以物理学为专业的研究者」，对应第 1 个义项：从事物理研究的人；句意为研究者把测量结果贴到公告板，同行围绕误差来源展开争论。画面要点：黑板上的公式、粉笔、拆开的钟表与磁铁；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 物理学家；物理学研究者（可数，复数指一群从业者）

derivatives.zh: 物理学（由希腊语中表示「自然之物」的复数形式经拉丁语传入，指研究物质与运动的学科）
物理的；身体的（学科名词加形容词后缀，指属于物质世界的，后也指人的身体）
在物理上；身体上（形容词加副词后缀，指从物质或身体的角度）
天体物理（表示「星体」的前缀与物理学复合，指用物理方法研究天体）

senses.title: A researcher of matter and energy
senses.titleCN: 研究物质与能量的研究者
senses.definition: a person whose work is to study matter, motion, energy and the forces between them
senses.definitionCN: 以研究物质、运动、能量及其间的作用力为工作的人
senses.example: A researcher pinned a new set of measurements to the board in the corridor, and colleagues gathered to argue about the source of error that the physicist had reported.
senses.exampleCN: 一位研究者把新的测量结果贴到走廊的公告板上，同行围过来争论他所报告的误差来源。
senses.why: The word joins the name of the discipline to a suffix for a practitioner, so it names a person by the field he works in.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把学科名称与表从业者的后缀连在一起，因此它用一个人所从事的领域来命名他。

senses.title: The theorist
senses.definition: one who works mainly with mathematical models and predictions rather than with apparatus
senses.definitionCN: 主要用数学模型与预测工作、而不是与仪器打交道的人
senses.example: The theorist predicted a particle years before it was detected.
senses.exampleCN: 这位理论物理学家在粒子被探测到之前多年就预言了它。
senses.why: The discipline divides between those who write the equations and those who test them, and the same title covers both.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科分成写方程的人与检验方程的人，而同一个称谓覆盖两者。

senses.title: The experimentalist
senses.definition: one who designs instruments and measurements to test predictions or discover new effects
senses.definitionCN: 设计仪器与测量、以检验预言或发现新效应的人
senses.example: The experimentalist spent a decade building the detector.
senses.exampleCN: 这位实验物理学家花了十年建造探测器。
senses.why: A prediction that no one can measure remains a guess, so the title also belongs to the person who builds the test.
senses.whyCN: 无人能测量的预言仍然只是猜测，因此这个称谓也属于搭建检验的人。

senses.title: A specialist in a branch
senses.definition: a person who works in a named branch such as astrophysics, geophysics or particle physics
senses.definitionCN: 在天体物理、地球物理或粒子物理等具名分支中工作的人
senses.example: The astrophysicist studies how galaxies collide.
senses.exampleCN: 这位天体物理学家研究星系如何碰撞。
senses.why: The title combines with branch prefixes, so it multiplies into as many names as the subject has branches.
senses.whyCN: 这个称谓可以与分支前缀组合，因此它随学科的分支数量一同增殖。

senses.title: A teacher of the subject
senses.definition: a person who teaches physics in a school or university rather than working mainly in a laboratory
senses.definitionCN: 在学校或大学教物理、而非主要在实验室工作的人
senses.example: The physicist who taught the evening class wrote his own demonstrations.
senses.exampleCN: 教晚间课程的那位物理学家自己编写了演示实验。
senses.why: Teaching is part of the profession, and the same title covers the classroom as well as the bench.
senses.whyCN: 教学是这一职业的一部分，因此同一个称谓既覆盖实验室工作台，也覆盖教室。

senses.title: The natural philosopher in older use
senses.definition: a person who studied nature before the modern disciplines separated, often called a philosopher of nature
senses.definitionCN: 在现代各学科分化之前研究自然的人，常被称为自然哲学家
senses.example: The physicist of that era also wrote on theology and optics.
senses.exampleCN: 那个时代的物理学家也写神学与光学方面的著作。
senses.why: The word arrived in the nineteenth century, and older figures are often given the title retrospectively even though they used a different one.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在十九世纪才出现，较早的人物尽管自用别的称谓，仍常被追授这一称号。

senses.title: One who carries the method elsewhere
senses.titleCN: 把物理方法带到其他领域的人
senses.definition: a researcher trained in physics who applies its methods to biology, medicine, finance or computing
senses.definitionCN: 受过物理训练、却把其方法用于生物、医学、金融或计算领域的研究者
senses.example: The physicist now models how proteins fold.
senses.exampleCN: 这位物理学家现在为蛋白质折叠建立模型。
senses.why: A method travels with its practitioner, so the title can follow a person into a field that is not physics.
senses.whyCN: 方法随从业者一同迁移，因此这个称谓可以跟着一个人进入并非物理的领域。

senses.title: The writer who explains the subject
senses.titleCN: 面向公众解释物理的写作者
senses.definition: a person who makes the subject intelligible to non-specialists through books, lectures or broadcasts
senses.definitionCN: 通过书籍、讲座或广播使非专业者也能理解这门学科的人
senses.example: The physicist's popular books brought the subject to a wide audience.
senses.exampleCN: 这位物理学家的通俗著作把该学科带给了广大读者。
senses.why: When a field becomes specialised, someone must translate it outward, and the title follows that work too.
senses.whyCN: 当一门学科高度专门化，总得有人把它向外翻译，这个称谓也随这份工作延伸。

intro.en: Physicist is physics plus the Greek-derived suffix for a practitioner. The word was proposed in 1840 by William Whewell to distinguish a student of physics from a physician; that date is recorded rather than approximate.
intro.cn: physicist 由 physics 加希腊语来源的从业者后缀构成。这个词由威廉·休厄尔于 1840 年提出，用以把研究物理的人与医生区分开；这个年代是确切记载，而非约数。

items.en: Phusis 'nature' named the way things grow and behave on their own, and it is the ultimate root of the whole family.
items.cn: phusis 意为「自然」，指事物自行生长与表现的方式，是整个词族的最终词根。

items.en: Ta phusika 'natural things' was the title of Aristotle's treatises and became the name of the study of nature.
items.cn: ta phusika 意为「自然之物」，是亚里士多德诸篇的标题，后来成为研究自然的学问的名称。

items.en: Latin physica carried the subject into English, where the singular physic first meant medicine and the plural came to mean natural science.
items.cn: 拉丁语 physica 把这门学问带入英语；在英语中单数形式先指医学，复数形式后来指自然科学。

items.en: The suffix for a practitioner came through Latin and French; it marks a person devoted to a field, as in artist or chemist.
items.cn: 表示从业者的后缀经拉丁语与法语传入；它标示献身于某一领域的人，如艺术家或化学家。

items.en: William Whewell proposed physicist in 1840 for a student of physics, since physician already meant a healer. The date is recorded.
items.cn: 威廉·休厄尔在 1840 年提出用 physicist 指研究物理的人，因为 physician 已被医生占用。这个年代有确切记载。

items.en: As physics became a paid profession in universities and laboratories, the word settled into its present sense of a trained researcher or teacher.
items.cn: 随着物理学在大学与实验室中成为有薪职业，这个词稳定为现今「受过训练的研究者或教师」之义。

note.en: The first group shares the Greek word for nature or looks close to the title; the second group gives near alternatives for a person who studies the world.
note.cn: 第一组共享希腊语中表示「自然」的词，或与这个称谓形近；第二组是「研究世界的人」的近义替代。

entries.definition: A doctor of medicine; it comes from the same root but kept the older medical sense, which is why the two titles are constantly confused.
entries.definitionCN: 医生；它出自同一词根，却保留了较早的医学义，因此这两个称谓常被混淆。

entries.definition: The science of matter and motion; the entry word adds a suffix for the person, so one is the subject and the other the practitioner.
entries.definitionCN: 研究物质与运动的科学；本词加上表人的后缀，因此一个是学科，一个是从业者。

entries.definition: Of matter or the body; it describes things, while the entry word names a person.
entries.definitionCN: 物质的或身体的；它描述事物，而本词命名人。

entries.definition: The shape and strength of a body; it is close in spelling but names a frame, not a profession.
entries.definitionCN: 身体的形态与力量；它拼写相近，却命名体格而不是职业。

entries.definition: Anyone who works in a systematic science; the entry word is one kind of scientist, defined by its field.
entries.definitionCN: 任何从事系统科学研究的人；本词是科学家的一种，由所属领域来界定。

entries.definition: A person who investigates a question systematically, in any field; it names the activity rather than the discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 在任何领域系统探究某一问题的人；它命名活动，而不是学科。

entries.definition: The older name for a student of nature before disciplines separated; it is the historical counterpart of the entry word.
entries.definitionCN: 各学科分化之前研究自然者的旧称；它是本词在历史上的对应称谓。

entries.definition: A person devoted to one narrow area; it stresses depth in a corner rather than training in a whole field.
entries.definitionCN: 专攻某一狭小领域的人；它强调在某个角落的深度，而不是对整个领域的训练。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Greek word for nature, the practitioner suffix, a recorded coinage and real branch titles.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：希腊语中表示「自然」的词、表从业者的后缀、有确切记载的造词与真实的分支称谓。

normal.en: The word is the field plus a suffix for a person, so it always answers 'who works in physics'.
normal.cn: 这个词是学科名称加表人的后缀，因此它总是回答「谁在搞物理」。

normal.en: The family runs physics, physical, physically and astrophysics.
normal.cn: 同族词包括物理学、物理的、在物理上与天体物理。

normal.en: The recorded date is 1840, when the title was proposed to keep it apart from the word for a doctor.
normal.cn: 确切记载的年代是 1840 年，当时提出这个称谓是为了把它与表示医生的词分开。

normal.en: The title splits into theorist and experimentalist, and multiplies with branch prefixes.
normal.cn: 这个称谓分成理论者与实验者，并随分支前缀一同增殖。

normal.en: A method can travel, so a person trained in the field may end up modelling proteins or markets.
normal.cn: 方法可以迁移，因此受过该领域训练的人可能去为蛋白质或市场建模。

abstract.en: Picture a figure at a blackboard with chalk in hand, a dismantled clock and a magnet on the bench behind.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在黑板前手持粉笔，身后的工作台上放着拆开的钟表和一块磁铁。

abstract.en: Picture two people facing the same equation from opposite sides, one writing it and one testing it.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人从两侧面对同一个方程，一个写下它，一个检验它。

abstract.en: Picture a name tag that changes its first half as its wearer moves from stars to rocks to cells.
abstract.cn: 想象一张名牌，佩带者从星体转到岩石再转到细胞时，它的前半截随之改变。

examples.en: The physicist argued that the anomaly was a fault in the detector.
examples.cn: 这位物理学家主张，那个异常是探测器的故障。

examples.en: Two physicists shared the prize for the same prediction.
examples.cn: 两位物理学家因同一项预言分享了该奖。

examples.en: As a physicist she was trained to distrust any number without an error bar.
examples.cn: 作为物理学家，她受过的训练让她不信任任何没有误差范围的数字。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费兹希斯特」——先想「物理」，再想「人」：站在黑板前写公式、在台前测数据的那一位。

root: 希腊语 phusis「自然」→ phusika「自然之物」→ 拉丁语 physica「自然科学」→ 英语 physics；再加希腊语来源、经拉丁语与法语传入的从业者后缀 -ist，构成 physicist。该词由威廉·休厄尔于 1840 年提出，年代有确切记载。

sensesIntro.en: Eight readings describe one person from different angles: the profession, the theorist and the experimentalist, the branch specialist and the one who carries the method elsewhere, the teacher and the popular writer, and the older natural philosopher whose title is applied retrospectively.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从不同角度描述同一种人：职业本身、理论者与实验者、分支专家与把方法带到别处的人、教师与通俗写作者，以及被追授旧称的自然哲学家。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a trained person at a blackboard, with instruments waiting on the bench behind.
core.cn: 核心意象：站在黑板前受过训练的人，身后的工作台上放着仪器。

branches.en: THE PROFESSION: a person defined by the field he works in.
branches.cn: 职业：以所从事领域来界定的人。

branches.en: TWO HANDS: the one who writes the equations, and the one who builds the test.
branches.cn: 两只手：写方程的人，与搭建检验的人。

branches.en: BRANCH AND CROSSING: a named specialism, and a method carried into another discipline.
branches.cn: 分支与跨越：具名的专长，以及被带进另一学科的方法。

branches.en: TEACHER AND WRITER: the classroom, and the translation of the field for the public.
branches.cn: 教师与写作者：教室里的传授，以及面向公众的转译。

branches.en: ANCESTOR: the natural philosopher, given the title after the fact.
branches.cn: 祖先：事后被授予这一称号的自然哲学家。

intro.en: The title is built from the Greek-rooted name of the field plus a suffix for a practitioner; the same suffix also forms artist, chemist and scientist.
intro.cn: 这个称谓由希腊语词根的学科名称加表从业者的后缀构成；同一个后缀也构成艺术家、化学家与科学家。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms below belong to the field half of the title; the person suffix reached English through Latin and French but is Greek in origin.
latinIntro.cn: 下列拉丁形式属于称谓中「学科」的那一半；表人的后缀经拉丁语与法语传入英语，但源自希腊语。

senses.title: The science of matter and motion
senses.titleCN: 研究物质与运动的学科
senses.definition: the branch of science that studies matter, energy, motion, forces and the structure of the universe
senses.definitionCN: 研究物质、能量、运动、力以及宇宙结构的那门科学
senses.example: In the laboratory students timed a pendulum and measured the focal length of a lens, hoping that one law of physics would explain both.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室里，学生记录单摆周期、测量透镜焦距，希望同一条物理定律能解释两者。
senses.why: The Greek source named 'natural things', so the discipline begins as the study of whatever happens by nature rather than by human arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语来源意为「自然之物」，因此这门学科起初研究的是依本性而非依人造安排发生的一切。

senses.title: How a particular thing works
senses.titleCN: 某具体事物的运作原理
senses.definition: the physical principles behind a device, a sport or a natural event
senses.definitionCN: 某个装置、某项运动或某种自然现象背后的物理原理
senses.example: The coach explained the physics of a spinning ball.
senses.exampleCN: 教练讲解了旋转球的物理原理。
senses.why: The name of a whole discipline can be applied to one small case, because every case is an instance of the same laws.
senses.whyCN: 整门学科的名称可以用在一个小案例上，因为每个案例都是同一批定律的实例。

senses.title: Classical mechanics in practice
senses.definition: the part of the subject dealing with bodies moving well below the speed of light, as formulated before relativity
senses.definitionCN: 研究远低于光速运动的物体、在相对论之前已成体系的那部分内容
senses.example: The bridge design was checked with classical physics.
senses.exampleCN: 桥梁设计用经典物理作了校核。
senses.why: The old core of the subject kept the plain name, so 'physics' often means the mechanics of ordinary speeds and sizes.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科旧有的核心保留了这个朴素的名字，因此「物理」常指日常速度与尺度下的力学。

senses.title: Relativity and the quantum
senses.titleCN: 相对论与量子层面的现代物理
senses.definition: the parts of the subject that describe very fast, very massive or very small systems
senses.definitionCN: 描述极快、极重或极小系统的那部分内容
senses.example: Modern physics begins where the classical laws stop working.
senses.exampleCN: 现代物理从经典定律失效之处开始。
senses.why: When the old laws failed at the extremes, the same word had to cover the theories that replaced them.
senses.whyCN: 当旧定律在极端情形下失效，同一个词就必须覆盖取而代之的新理论。

senses.title: Branch subjects built on the name
senses.titleCN: 以该词构成的各分支学科
senses.definition: fields formed by joining a prefix to the subject, such as the physics of stars, of the earth or of living things
senses.definitionCN: 在学科名称前加前缀构成的领域，如研究星体、地球或生物的那几门
senses.example: Astrophysics applies the methods of physics to stars.
senses.exampleCN: 天体物理把物理学的方法用于星体。
senses.why: A method that works on one scale invites use on every scale, so the name becomes a suffix for whole new fields.
senses.whyCN: 在一个尺度上有效的方法会被用到所有尺度，于是这个名字成了新领域的后缀。

senses.title: A course and a textbook
senses.titleCN: 一门课程与一本教科书
senses.definition: the school or university subject as it is taught, examined and written up
senses.definitionCN: 在学校或大学里被教授、考核与编写成书的那门科目
senses.example: She took physics in her first year and chemistry in her second.
senses.exampleCN: 她第一年修物理，第二年修化学。
senses.why: A discipline becomes a subject when it acquires a syllabus, and the same noun then names the room, the hour and the book.
senses.whyCN: 一门学问获得教学大纲后就成了科目，同一个名词于是也命名教室、课时与课本。

senses.title: The mechanism behind an outcome
senses.definition: the practical cause-and-effect chain that makes something happen, used in ordinary speech
senses.definitionCN: 使某事发生的实际因果链条，用于日常口语
senses.example: The physics of the market is not the same as the physics of a bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 市场的运作机制与桥梁的运作机制并不相同。
senses.why: Speakers borrow the word whenever they want to say that something has a mechanism rather than a mystery.
senses.whyCN: 说话者借用这个词，是想说某事有一套机制，而不是一个谜。

senses.title: Natural philosophy in older use
senses.definition: the older name for the study of nature, before the modern sciences separated
senses.definitionCN: 现代各门科学分化之前，研究自然的学问的旧称
senses.example: Newton wrote his great work under the old name for physics.
senses.exampleCN: 牛顿以物理学的旧称写下他的巨著。
senses.why: Before disciplines divided, the study of nature was one subject, and its old title is still visible in the word's ancestry.
senses.whyCN: 在各学科分化之前，对自然的研究是一门学问，它的旧称仍可见于这个词的来历。

intro.en: Physics comes from Greek phusis 'nature', through Latin physica 'natural things'. English first used physic for medicine, and later took physics for natural science, so the two forms parted company.
intro.cn: physics 出自希腊语 phusis「自然」，经由拉丁语 physica「自然之物」传入。英语先用 physic 指医学，后来用 physics 指自然科学，两种形式从此分道。

items.en: Phuein 'to grow, bring forth' is the verb at the root of the family, and it describes what comes into being by itself.
items.cn: phuein 意为「生长、产生」，是这个词族的根动词，描述自行生成之物。

items.en: Phusis 'nature' named the way things grow and behave on their own, as opposed to what is made by craft.
items.cn: phusis 意为「自然」，指事物自行生长与表现的方式，与人以技艺造作之物相对。

items.en: Ta phusika 'natural things' was the title of Aristotle's treatises on nature, and the phrase became the name of the subject.
items.cn: ta phusika 意为「自然之物」，是亚里士多德论自然诸篇的标题，这个说法后来成为学科名称。

items.en: Latin physica, a neuter plural, named natural science, and it passed into English in that form.
items.cn: 拉丁语 physica 是中性复数，指自然科学，并以这一形式进入英语。

items.en: In English physic first meant the art of healing, because medicine studied the natural body; that sense survives in the word for a doctor.
items.cn: 在英语中，physic 起初指医术，因为医学研究的是自然身体；这一意思残留在表示医生的那个词里。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the plural form was used for natural science, while the singular stayed with medicine. The date is approximate.
items.cn: 自十六世纪起，复数形式用来指自然科学，单数形式则留在医学。年代为约数。

note.en: The first group shares the Greek word for nature but has split into medicine, body build and the adjective; the second group places the subject among neighbouring sciences.
note.cn: 第一组共享希腊语中表示「自然」的词，但已分成医学、体格与形容词；第二组把这门学科放进相邻的科学之中。

entries.definition: The art of healing, now archaic; it is the same source word, but it named medicine rather than the science of matter.
entries.definitionCN: 医术，现已古旧；它是同一个来源词，但命名的是医学，而不是研究物质的科学。

entries.definition: The shape and strength of a person's body; it comes from the same Greek root but through French, and names a frame rather than a field.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人身体的形态与力量；它出自同一希腊词根，但经法语传入，命名的是体格而不是学科。

entries.definition: Of matter or the body, as opposed to the mental; it describes a kind of thing, while the entry word names a science.
entries.definitionCN: 物质的或身体的，与心理的相对；它描述一类事物，而本词命名一门科学。

entries.definition: A person trained in the subject; the suffix marks the practitioner rather than the field.
entries.definitionCN: 受过该学科训练的人；后缀标示从业者，而不是领域。

entries.definition: Any science of the physical world, including biology, chemistry and geology; the entry word is one member of it.
entries.definitionCN: 研究物理世界的任何科学，包括生物学、化学与地质学；本词是其中一员。

entries.definition: The study of bodies and the forces acting on them; it is a branch of the entry subject rather than a synonym for it.
entries.definitionCN: 研究物体及作用其上的力；它是本学科的一个分支，而不是同义词。

entries.definition: Sciences of non-living systems, such as physics and chemistry; the phrase is broader and excludes biology.
entries.definitionCN: 研究非生命系统的科学，如物理与化学；这个说法更宽，但不包括生物学。

entries.definition: Organised knowledge obtained by observation and experiment; it covers every discipline, of which the entry word is one.
entries.definitionCN: 经观察与实验获得的系统知识；它覆盖所有学科，本词是其中之一。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Greek word for nature, the Latin plural for natural things, real derived words and real branch names.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：希腊语中表示「自然」的词、拉丁语中表示「自然之物」的复数、真实派生词与真实分支名称。

normal.en: The root means nature, so the subject begins as the study of what happens by itself.
normal.cn: 词根意为「自然」，因此这门学科起初研究自行发生之事。

normal.en: The family runs physical, physically, physicist, astrophysics and metaphysics.
normal.cn: 同族词包括物理的、身体上、物理学家、天体物理与形而上学。

normal.en: The older singular meant medicine, which is why a doctor and a scientist share a root.
normal.cn: 较早的单数形式指医学，所以医生与科学家共有一个词根。

normal.en: The subject splits into classical and modern halves, and into branches named by a prefix.
normal.cn: 这门学科分成经典与现代两半，也分成由前缀命名的各分支。

normal.en: A pendulum and a lens obey the same laws, which is the promise the word makes.
normal.cn: 单摆与透镜服从同一批定律，这正是这个词所许诺的事。

abstract.en: Picture a pendulum at the top of its arc, a thermometer beside it and a prism splitting light, all waiting to be measured.
abstract.cn: 想象一只摆锤停在弧线的最高点，旁边是温度计，还有一块分光的棱镜，都在等着被测量。

abstract.en: Picture a single law written on a card, held up against two completely different experiments.
abstract.cn: 想象一张卡片上写着一条定律，被举到两组完全不同的实验面前。

abstract.en: Picture a tree whose trunk is nature and whose branches are named after stars, rocks and living cells.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵树，树干是「自然」，枝干则以星体、岩石与活细胞命名。

examples.en: The physics of the atmosphere explains why the balloon rose so fast.
examples.cn: 大气的物理原理解释了气球为何上升得那么快。

examples.en: He studied physics before turning to the history of science.
examples.cn: 他先修物理，后来转向科学史。

examples.en: No law of physics forbids the machine, only the cost does.
examples.cn: 没有物理定律禁止这台机器，只是成本不允许。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费兹克斯」——「费」力气去「测」：摆锤、棱镜、温度计，量的都是同一件事，这就是物理。

root: 希腊语 phuein「生长、产生」→ phusis「自然」→ ta phusika「自然之物」→ 拉丁语 physica「自然科学」→ 英语 physics。较早的英语形式 physic 指医学，后复数形式专指自然科学；这一分开的年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight readings radiate from one discipline. The subject itself comes first, then the practical physics of a single thing, then its classical core, its modern extensions, its branch subjects, its life as a course, its looser use for any mechanism, and its older name as natural philosophy.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一门学科辐射开。先是学科本身，其次是某件具体事物的运作原理，再其次是它的经典内核、现代扩展、各分支学科、作为课程的存在、泛指任何机制的宽松用法，以及它作为「自然之学」的旧名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a swinging pendulum beside instruments that all measure the same interaction.
core.cn: 核心意象：摆动的摆锤，旁边是一同测量同一种相互作用的仪器。

branches.en: THE SUBJECT: the whole discipline, and the same thing as a course and a textbook.
branches.cn: 学科：整体学问，以及它作为课程与教科书的存在。

branches.en: THE MECHANISM: how one thing works, and the everyday use of the word for any causal chain.
branches.cn: 机制：某物如何运作，以及日常口语中用这个词泛指任何因果链。

branches.en: CLASSICAL CORE: bodies at ordinary speeds, governed by the older laws.
branches.cn: 经典内核：日常速度下的物体，由较早的定律支配。

branches.en: MODERN EDGE: what happens at extreme speed, mass or smallness.
branches.cn: 现代边缘：在极端速度、质量或微小尺度下发生的事。

branches.en: BRANCHES AND ANCESTOR: prefix-named fields, and the older single study of nature.
branches.cn: 分支与祖先：以前缀命名的各领域，以及较早的那门统一的自然之学。

intro.en: The family comes from a Greek verb for growing, through a Greek noun for nature and a Latin plural for natural things; English then built adjectives, persons and whole branch names on it.
intro.cn: 这个词族出自一个表示「生长」的希腊动词，经由表示「自然」的希腊名词与表示「自然之物」的拉丁复数，英语再在其上构成形容词、人物名词与整批分支名称。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms below are themselves borrowed from Greek; they carried the subject into English and also left the older word for medicine.
latinIntro.cn: 下列拉丁形式本身借自希腊语；它们把这门学科带入英语，也留下了表示医学的那个较早的词。

items.meaning: the science of matter and motion
items.meaningCN: 研究物质与运动的科学
items.example: Physics explains why the apple falls.
items.exampleCN: 物理学的解释了苹果为何下落。

items.example: The physical world obeys measurable laws.
items.exampleCN: 物质世界服从可测量的定律。
这项任务对体力要求很高。

items.example: The physicist measured the decay rate.
items.exampleCN: 那位物理学家测量了衰变率。

items.meaning: the art of healing, now archaic
items.example: The old physic book lists herbal remedies.
items.exampleCN: 那本旧医书列着草药方。

items.meaning: the physics of stars and space
items.meaningCN: 研究星体与太空的物理
items.exampleCN: 天体物理研究恒星如何形成。

items.example: Geophysics maps the rock beneath the city.
items.exampleCN: 地球物理测绘城市地下的岩层。
生物物理为蛋白质折叠建立模型。

items.meaning: the study of being, placed after the physical treatises
items.meaningCN: 研究存在的学问，原编排在物理诸篇之后
items.example: The question belongs to metaphysics, not to physics.
items.exampleCN: 这个问题属于形而上学，而不是物理学。

definition_en: a large keyboard instrument whose strings are struck by hammers; also the skill of playing it and its part in a piece of music

scene: 琴房的门关着，木地板被午后的光照得发亮，一个孩子把手指悬在黑白琴键上方不敢落下。The piano stood open in the corner, waiting for the first note.
sceneCN: 这里 piano 指「钢琴」（第 1 个义项：那台键盘乐器）；句意为钢琴开着盖立在角落，等着第一个音。图中可辨识物件：黑白琴键、支起的琴盖、谱架。

senses.title: The keyboard instrument
senses.definition: a large musical instrument with a row of black and white keys that send hammers to strike strings inside a wooden case
senses.definitionCN: 一种大型乐器，黑白琴键带动木箱内的琴槌敲击琴弦发声
senses.example: The piano stood open in the corner of the room.
senses.exampleCN: 钢琴开着盖立在房间角落。
senses.why: Italian piano meant soft, and the instrument's full name pianoforte said it could sound both soft and strong, which was exactly what the older harpsichord could not do.
senses.whyCN: 意大利语 piano 意为轻柔，这件乐器的全名 pianoforte 是在说它既能弱也能强，而这正是旧式羽管键琴做不到的事。

senses.title: The skill or subject of playing it
senses.definition: the art or school subject of playing this instrument, as in studying piano at a conservatory
senses.definitionCN: 演奏这件乐器的技艺或学校科目，如音乐学院里的钢琴专业
senses.example: He studied piano for ten years before he ever performed in public.
senses.exampleCN: 他学了十年钢琴才第一次公开演出。
senses.why: English lets the name of an instrument stand for the skill practised on it, so piano becomes a subject you can study, teach, or take an exam in.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许乐器名直接指在这件乐器上练出来的技艺，于是 piano 成了一门可以学、可以教、可以考试的科目。

senses.title: The piano part in a score or ensemble
senses.definition: the line or part written for the piano in a score, especially when it plays alongside other instruments
senses.definitionCN: 总谱中写给钢琴的那一行或那一声部，尤指与其他乐器合奏时
senses.example: The piano enters softly under the strings in the second movement.
senses.exampleCN: 第二乐章里，钢琴在弦乐之下轻轻进入。
senses.why: Once a score lists instruments by name, each named staff can be called by its instrument, so the piano printed on the page becomes the piano heard in the hall.
senses.whyCN: 总谱一旦按乐器名称分列各行，每一行就能直接用乐器名来称呼，于是印在纸上的「钢琴」变成了大厅里听到的钢琴声部。

intro.en: Piano is a shortened Italian phrase: the full name of the instrument described its ability to sound soft as well as loud.
intro.cn: piano 是意大利语短语的缩略：这件乐器的全名描述的是它既能弱也能强。

items.en: Planus meant flat, level, or plain, and it is the distant source of the Italian word for soft and smooth.
items.cn: planus 意为平的、平坦的、平实的，是意大利语中表示柔和、平滑那个词的远源。

items.en: Italian piano meant soft or smooth, and musicians used it as a direction to play quietly.
items.cn: 意大利语 piano 意为轻柔、平滑，乐师用它作「轻声演奏」的指示。

items.en: Pianoforte joined piano, soft, with forte, strong, to name a harpsichord-like instrument that could do both.
items.cn: pianoforte 把表示「弱」的 piano 与表示「强」的 forte 拼在一起，用来命名一种既能弱又能强、类似羽管键琴的乐器。

items.en: English borrowed the instrument and shortened the long name to piano, which then became the everyday word.
items.cn: 英语借来这件乐器，并把长名缩短为 piano，随后它成了日常说法。

items.en: Modern English uses piano for the instrument, for the skill, and for the part, while the full name survives mostly in formal writing.
items.cn: 现代英语用 piano 指乐器、技艺与声部，而旧的全名大多只留在正式文字里。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Italian word and the forms built on it; the near-meaning group gathers other keyboard instruments.
note.cn: 形近组沿着这个意大利语词及其派生形式排列；近义组收其他键盘乐器。

entries.definition: A person who plays the piano, often as a profession.
entries.definitionCN: 弹钢琴的人，常指职业钢琴家。

entries.definition: The full eighteenth-century name of the instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 这件乐器在十八世纪的全名。

entries.definition: A musical direction meaning very soft.
entries.definitionCN: 音乐术语：极弱地。

entries.definition: The art or technique of piano playing.
entries.definitionCN: 钢琴演奏的艺术或技巧。

entries.definition: A large keyboard instrument that makes sound by driving air through pipes.
entries.definitionCN: 靠气流通过音管发声的大型键盘乐器；管风琴。

entries.definition: An older keyboard instrument whose strings are plucked rather than struck.
entries.definitionCN: 更早的键盘乐器，琴弦被拨动而非被敲击；羽管键琴。

entries.definition: A row of keys on an instrument, or an electronic instrument built around such keys.
entries.definitionCN: 乐器上的一排琴键，或围绕琴键制成的电子乐器。

normalIntro.en: The word began life as an Italian direction for soft playing, and the instrument took that word as its name.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词原本是意大利语里「轻声演奏」的指示，乐器后来把这个词当成了自己的名字。

normal.en: Piano in Italian means soft, so the marking piano on a score still tells a player to play quietly.
normal.cn: 意大利语 piano 意为轻柔，所以谱面上的 piano 记号至今仍在告诉演奏者放轻。

normal.en: The full name pianoforte joined soft and strong, because this instrument could change volume in a way the harpsichord could not.
normal.cn: 全名 pianoforte 把「弱」与「强」拼在一起，因为这件乐器能改变音量，而羽管键琴不能。

normal.en: English cut the long name down to piano, and the short form is now the ordinary word in every shop that sells one.
normal.cn: 英语把长名砍成 piano，这个短形式如今成了每家琴行里的日常说法。

normal.en: Pianist adds -ist to piano, and the stress moves to the first syllable even though the spelling keeps the o.
normal.cn: pianist 在 piano 后加 -ist，重音移到第一个音节，但拼写里仍留着那个 o。

normal.en: The plural is pianos, not pianoes, because the word came from Italian and simply takes an s.
normal.cn: 复数是 pianos 而不是 pianoes，因为这个词来自意大利语，直接加 s。

abstract.en: A word meaning soft became the name of an instrument that can be very loud, because its novelty was the power to be quiet.
abstract.cn: 一个意为「轻柔」的词，成了一台能很响的乐器的名字，因为它的新鲜处正在于能安静下来。

abstract.en: Eighty-eight keys, one short word: the name grew shorter as the instrument grew common.
abstract.cn: 八十八个琴键，一个短词：乐器越普及，名字就越短。

abstract.en: The same word names the object, the skill and the line in the score, since all three begin at one keyboard.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指那件东西，也指那门技艺和谱面上的那一行，因为三者都从同一排琴键开始。

examples.en: The piano stood open in the corner of the room.
examples.cn: 钢琴开着盖立在房间角落。

examples.en: She has her piano lesson every Thursday afternoon.
examples.cn: 她每周四下午上钢琴课。

examples.en: The piano enters softly under the strings.
examples.cn: 钢琴在弦乐之下轻轻进入。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮阿诺」——琴键一按，声音轻得像耳语，piano 本来正是「轻柔」的意思。

root: 意大利语 piano（轻柔、平滑）源自拉丁语 planus（平的、平实的）；pianoforte 由 piano 与 forte（强）合成，英语缩略为 piano。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the instrument that can be soft and strong; from the object come the skill practised on it and the part it plays in a score.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是那件能弱能强的键盘乐器；由这件实物分出在它上面练成的技艺，以及它在总谱里担任的声部。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: black and white keys running away under a lamp, the lid propped open.
core.cn: 核心意象：灯下一排黑白琴键向远处延伸，琴盖被支起。

branches.en: a wooden case with its lid propped open
branches.cn: 琴盖支起的木制琴箱

branches.en: a child's hand hovering above the keys before the first lesson
branches.cn: 第一堂课之前悬在琴键上方的小手

branches.en: a practice room heard through a closed door
branches.cn: 隔着关着的门听见的练琴声

branches.cn: 三人合奏，其中一人在键盘前

intro.en: A Latin adjective for flat lies behind the Italian word for soft, and the instrument's double name was later cut in half.
intro.cn: 拉丁语中表示「平」的形容词是意大利语「轻柔」一词的来源，而乐器的双名后来被砍掉了一半。

latinIntro.en: Italian piano goes back to Latin planus, flat or plain, so the Latin entry belongs to the same family.
latinIntro.cn: 意大利语 piano 可追到拉丁语 planus（平的、平实的），所以这条拉丁词与它同属一族。

senses.title: A part broken or cut from something larger
senses.definition: a part separated from a whole, especially one small enough to hold or to see as a single unit
senses.definitionCN: 从整体上分离出来的一部分，尤指小到可以拿在手里或单独看见的一块
senses.example: She picked up the largest piece of the broken bowl.
senses.exampleCN: 她捡起碎碗上最大的那一块。
senses.why: Medieval Latin petia named a fragment, and English took the word with that broken-off shape already inside it, so the first sense is the shard rather than the whole.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪拉丁语 petia 本指碎片，英语借来时，「从整体上断下来的一块」这个形状已经装在词里，所以最早的义项是碎片而非整体。

senses.title: A single work of art, music, or writing
senses.definition: one complete work, especially a short musical composition, a painting, or a short text
senses.definitionCN: 一件完整的作品，尤指短小的乐曲、一幅画或一段短文
senses.example: The band played a new piece at the end of the set.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队在演出末尾演奏了一首新作品。
senses.why: A work is also a unit that can be counted and handed over, so the noun that counted fragments came to count finished works, each treated as one whole.
senses.whyCN: 作品同样是可以清点、可以交到别人手里的一个单位，于是原本数碎块的名词也用来数成品，每一件都被当作一个整体。

senses.title: One of the objects moved in a board game
senses.definition: one of the small objects that a player moves on a board, as in chess or draughts
senses.definitionCN: 棋手在棋盘上移动的小物件之一，如国际象棋或跳棋中的棋子
senses.example: He moved a single piece and the whole game turned.
senses.exampleCN: 他挪动了一枚棋子，整盘棋就变了。
senses.why: A game set is a collection of small separate units, and each one is literally a piece taken out of the box, which is why the word needed no stretching here.
senses.whyCN: 一副棋就是一小堆彼此分开的小单位，每一枚本来就是从盒子里取出来的一块，所以这个词在这里根本不必引申。

senses.title: To join parts into a whole
senses.definition: to put the separate parts of something together until they form a whole, often by patient work
senses.definitionCN: 把某物分开的各个部分合在一起，直到形成整体，常需耐心
senses.example: They pieced the torn map back together on the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在地板上把撕破的地图重新拼好。
senses.why: The verb reverses the noun: what was broken into pieces is put back, and the word now watches the fragments travel toward a whole instead of away from it.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词的方向倒过来：被分成块的东西重新合起来，这个词现在看着碎块朝整体走，而不是从整体散开。

intro.en: Piece came through Old French from a medieval Latin word for a fragment, and that word's own earlier origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: piece 经古法语来自中世纪拉丁语中表示碎片的一个词，而那个词更早的来源并不确定。

items.en: Medieval Latin petia or petium meant a piece or fragment, but its earlier origin is uncertain and a Gaulish source is often suggested.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 petia 或 petium 意为一块、碎片，但它更早的来源不确定，常有人推测来自高卢语。

items.en: Old French piece named a part, a fragment, or a coin, and carried the word into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语 piece 指一部分、碎片或一枚钱币，诺曼时期之后把这个词带进英语。

items.en: Middle English piece could mean a fragment, a share, or a particular item, and the spelling settled without the French accent.
items.cn: 中古英语的 piece 可指碎片、份额或某一件事物，拼写逐渐定型，去掉了法语的变音记号。

items.en: By the sixteenth century a piece could be a work of art or music, because such a work is exactly one countable item.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，piece 已可指一件艺术品或一首乐曲，因为这样一件作品恰好就是一个可以清点的事项。

items.en: Modern English keeps the fragment at the centre and builds phrasal verbs such as piece together, where the fragments are put back.
items.cn: 现代英语仍以碎片为中心，并造出 piece together 这类短语动词，让碎片重新拼回去。

normal.en: Piece came from Old French, and the medieval Latin form behind it already meant a fragment.

normal.en: Piece together is the noun turned into a verb: the fragments are made to travel back into a whole.

normal.cn: peace 读音完全相同，但来自另一个词根，所以写的时候必须把两者分开。

normal.en: Apiece adds a to piece and means one for each, as in tickets at ten pounds apiece.
normal.cn: apiece 在 piece 前加 a，意为「每人一个」，如门票每张十英镑。

normal.en: A piece of music and a piece of news both use piece as a counter for one item, not as a fragment.
normal.cn: 「一首乐曲」与「一则消息」里的 piece 都是清点事项的量词用法，而不是碎片。

abstract.en: The same word counts a broken shard, a finished sonata and a chessman, because English counts parts and wholes with one noun.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既数碎瓷片，也数写完的奏鸣曲和一枚棋子，因为英语用一个名词同时数部分与整体。

abstract.en: To piece something together is to trust that the fragments still carry the shape of what they came from.
abstract.cn: 把东西拼起来，就是相信这些碎片仍然带着它们原来所属之物的形状。

abstract.en: A piece is always smaller than its whole, except when the whole is a work of art, and then the piece is the whole.
abstract.cn: 一块总比它的整体小，除非那个整体是一件作品，这时「一件」就等于整体。

senses.title: To make a hole with a sharp point
senses.definition: to push a sharp object into or through something so that it makes a hole
senses.definitionCN: 用尖锐的物体扎入或穿过某物，形成一个小孔
senses.example: The needle pierced the cloth cleanly.
senses.exampleCN: 针干净利落地穿过了布。
senses.why: Old French percer already meant to bore through, and behind it stands Latin pertundere, to beat a hole through something, so the image is a point forcing a passage rather than a light touch.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 percer 本就有钻孔、穿透之意，它背后是拉丁语 pertundere（把某物敲穿），所以这个词的底子是一个尖点硬开出一条通路，而不是轻轻擦过。

senses.title: To cut sharply through silence, light or air
senses.definition: to sound or shine so sharply that it seems to cut through the surrounding space
senses.definitionCN: 声音或光线极其尖锐，仿佛把周围的空间切开
senses.example: A siren pierced the fog above the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 一声警笛刺破了港口上方的雾。
senses.why: Once a point can pass through cloth, the same verb is lent to anything that crosses a whole space in one stroke, and sound and light are the things that cross a room fastest.
senses.whyCN: 既然一个尖点能穿过布，这个动词就被借去说任何一下子横穿整片空间的东西；声音和光横穿一间屋子最快，所以最先被借走，划破寂静的用法由此而来。

senses.title: To force its way in, as cold or a gaze does
senses.definition: to enter or reach someone in a sharp, penetrating way, said of cold, wind or a look
senses.definitionCN: 以尖锐、深入的方式进入或触及某人，多就寒冷、风或目光而言
senses.example: The wind pierced her thin coat within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 几分钟之内，风就扎透了她的薄外套。
senses.why: Cold and glances enter a body without any tool, yet the sensation is the same as a point going in, so the verb spreads from objects to sensations that behave like objects.
senses.whyCN: 寒冷和目光并没有带上任何工具，却同样钻进身体，感觉与一个尖点扎进去毫无二致，于是这个词从实物扩展到行为像实物的感受。

senses.title: To wound or move someone deeply
senses.definition: to affect someone with sudden sharp emotion, as if something had gone through them
senses.definitionCN: 以突然而尖锐的情绪击中某人，仿佛有东西穿过了他
senses.example: Her question pierced him more than any insult.
senses.exampleCN: 她那个问题比任何辱骂都更刺痛他。
senses.why: The physical hole becomes a hole in someone's composure: what enters is no longer a needle but a sentence, and the wound is felt without ever being seen.
senses.whyCN: 实物上的孔变成了一个人镇定上的孔：扎进去的不再是针，而是一句话，伤口感觉得到却始终看不见，这正是从刺穿到刺心的那一转。

intro.en: Pierce comes through Old French percer from a Latin verb of boring, and the whole family keeps the picture of a point beating its way through material.
intro.cn: pierce 经古法语 percer 上溯到一个表示钻孔的拉丁动词，整族词都保留着尖点把材料一点点打开的画面。

items.en: Tundere meant to beat or to strike, and it underlies a set of Latin verbs about hammering and pounding.
items.cn: tundere 意为敲打、击打，一整组表示锤击、舂打的拉丁动词都由它构成。

items.en: Adding per-, through, produced pertundere, to beat or bore a hole through something.
items.cn: 加上表示穿过的 per-，构成 pertundere，意为把某物敲穿、钻透。

items.en: The recorded route runs through a Vulgar Latin verb pertusiare, to pierce; it is generally taken as the reconstructed link to the French form.
items.cn: 有记录的路径经过俗拉丁语动词 pertusiare（刺穿）；一般认为它是通往法语形式的中间环节，属于重构形式。

items.en: Old French percer meant to bore through and was carried into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语 percer 意为钻孔、穿透，诺曼时期之后传入英语。

items.en: Middle English had the verb by the thirteenth century, first about weapons and wounds, later about sound, cold and feeling.
items.cn: 中古英语在十三世纪已有这个动词，最初说武器与伤口，后来才用于声音、寒冷与情绪。

note.en: The first group gathers words with the same Latin boring root or a nearly identical look; the second gathers verbs of cutting into, entering and passing through.
note.cn: 第一组收同一拉丁「钻孔」词根的词以及外形极近的词；第二组收表示扎入、进入与穿过的动词。

normalIntro.en: A Latin verb of beating and a French verb of boring meet in one word, and every sense still carries a point that opens a way.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「敲打」与法语的「钻孔」在同一个词里会合，每个义项都还带着一个把路打开的尖点。

normal.en: Per- means through and tundere means to beat, so to pierce is literally to beat a way through the material.
normal.cn: per- 意为穿过，tundere 意为敲打，所以 pierce 字面上就是把材料敲出一条通路。

normal.en: French percer dropped the Latin t and softened the ending, which is why English has pierce and not the longer Latin shape.
normal.cn: 法语 percer 丢掉了拉丁语的 t，又软化了词尾，英语因此得到 pierce，而不是那个更长的拉丁词形。

normal.en: The past tense and past participle are both pierced, with no doubling of the r and no change of vowel.
normal.cn: 过去式与过去分词都是 pierced，r 不双写，元音也不变。

normal.en: The -ing form leads a double life: as a participle it describes the action, as an adjective it describes a sound that seems to cut.
normal.cn: 加 -ing 的形式有双重身份：作分词时叙述动作，作形容词时形容一种仿佛会切割的声音。

normal.en: A pierced ear, a piercing cry and a piercing wind all keep the one image of something going straight through.
normal.cn: 打了耳洞的耳朵、刺耳的哭喊、刺骨的风，都守着同一个画面：有东西直穿而过。

abstract.en: A needle leaves a hole too small to see, yet the cloth is no longer whole; pierce names exactly that invisible change.
abstract.cn: 针留下的孔小得看不见，布却已经不完整；pierce 命名的正是这种看不见的改变。

abstract.en: A sound cuts nothing, but we say it pierces because attention is a fabric, and a loud noise tears it along one line.
abstract.cn: 声音其实什么也切不开，我们却说它刺穿，是因为注意力像一块布，巨响沿着一条线把它撕开。

abstract.en: The word travels from metal to voice to feeling, which shows how readily English gives pain and noise a sharp point.
abstract.cn: 这个词从金属走到声音，再走到感情，说明英语多愿意给痛感和噪音装上一个尖点。

scene: 冬天的广场上，一位老人把面包屑撒在脚边，灰羽的鸟一只接一只落下来。A lone pigeon walked between the benches as if it owned the square.
sceneCN: 这里是「鸽子」（第 1 个义项：泛指城市与乡间常见的鸽属鸟类）；句意为一只鸽子在长椅之间踱步，像广场归它所有。画面里是老人脚边落下的那一片灰羽。

derivatives.zh: 由 pigeon 与 hole 复合而成，本指鸽舍里的小格，引申为「分类格」以及动词「把……搁置归档」
由 pigeon 与 toe 的过去分词形式复合而成，形容脚尖向内、走路像鸽子的样子
由 pigeon 加表示场所的后缀 -ry 构成，义为「鸽舍；养鸽场」

senses.title: The bird itself
senses.definition: a plump grey bird with a small head and short legs, found in towns and in the countryside
senses.definitionCN: 一种体形丰满、头小、腿短的灰色鸟，城市与乡间都常见
senses.example: A pigeon pecked at the crumbs under the fountain.
senses.exampleCN: 一只鸽子在喷泉边啄食面包屑。
senses.why: Latin pipio named a young bird that cheeps, and English widened the word until it covered the whole grey species that shares our squares.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pipio 指会啾啾叫的雏鸟，英语把词义一步步放宽，直到覆盖与我们共用广场的这一整种灰鸟。

senses.title: A domesticated bird bred for messages or racing
senses.definition: a pigeon kept and trained by people, especially one bred to carry messages or to race home
senses.definitionCN: 由人饲养训练的鸽子，尤指培育来传信或竞翔归巢的个体
senses.example: He keeps a dozen pigeons on the roof and races them every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 他在屋顶养了十几只鸽子，每年春天都拿它们去比赛。
senses.why: Tame the bird and it becomes useful, so the same name shifts from the species to the working bird whose homing instinct can be trusted.
senses.whyCN: 把这种鸟驯养起来，它就有了用处，于是同一个名字从「这一种鸟」转到「能派上用场的鸟」，靠的正是它可信的归巢本能。

senses.title: A person who is easily fooled
senses.definition: a foolish person, or one who is easily tricked, used informally and often unkindly
senses.definitionCN: 愚蠢的人，或容易上当的人，属口语用法，常带不客气的意味
senses.example: They sold him a broken watch, and he never guessed he had been the pigeon.
senses.exampleCN: 他们卖给他一块坏表，他一直没察觉自己才是那个上当的人。
senses.why: A tame bird that comes to any hand offering grain is an easy image for a person who trusts too quickly, and the metaphor hardened into slang.
senses.whyCN: 一只被驯熟的鸟，谁伸手递谷子它就过去，正好比喻轻信的人，这个比喻后来凝固成俚语里的固定说法。

senses.title: A clay disc used as a shooting target
senses.definition: a round disc of baked clay thrown into the air as a moving target for shooters
senses.definitionCN: 用黏土烧成的圆盘，抛向空中作为射击者的活动靶
senses.example: The clay pigeon burst into dust the moment the shot rang out.
senses.exampleCN: 枪声一响，泥鸽靶就炸成了粉末。
senses.why: Shooters needed a cheap stand-in for the bird, named the disc after it, and kept the whole phrase even though nothing living is involved.
senses.whyCN: 射击者需要一个廉价的替代物来代替真鸟，就用鸟名来称呼这个圆盘，于是整个说法被保留下来，尽管其中已经没有活物。

intro.en: Pigeon goes back to a Latin word for a chirping nestling, which French and then English widened until it named the adult bird.
intro.cn: pigeon 可上溯到一个表示「啾啾叫的雏鸟」的拉丁词，经法语与英语两次放宽，最后用来指成鸟。

items.en: Pipire was a verb for the cheeping of small birds; it is generally taken to imitate the sound itself, and any earlier origin is uncertain.
items.cn: pipire 是表示小鸟啾啾叫的动词；一般认为它模仿叫声本身，更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Pipio named a young bird that cheeps, and it was used especially of nestlings and of young pigeons.
items.cn: pipio 指会啾啾叫的幼鸟，尤用于雏鸟与幼鸽。

items.en: Old French pijon meant a young pigeon and carried the word north into English usage.
items.cn: 古法语 pijon 意为幼鸽，把这个词带进了英语的使用范围。

items.en: Middle English spelled it pijon and then pigeon, and the meaning widened from the nestling to the adult bird.
items.cn: 中古英语先写作 pijon，后写作 pigeon，词义也从雏鸟放宽到成鸟。

items.en: Modern English adds the racing and message-carrying compounds, the clay target of shooting grounds, and the informal sense of a person easily fooled.
items.cn: 现代英语又添上竞翔与传信的复合词、射击场上的泥靶，以及「易受骗的人」这一口语义。

note.en: The first group gathers compounds and near-identical spellings around the bird; the second gathers other birds and words for a person who is easily deceived.
note.cn: 第一组收围绕这种鸟的复合词与拼写极近的词；第二组收其他鸟类，以及表示易受骗之人的词。

entries.definition: A small compartment in a desk or a rack, and by extension the act of filing something away for later.
entries.definitionCN: 书桌或架子上的小格子，引申为把某事归档、搁置起来。

entries.definition: Walking with the feet turned inward, in the way the bird's legs are set.
entries.definitionCN: 走路时脚尖向内，如同这种鸟的腿势。

entries.definition: Colouring matter used in paint or ink; it only looks similar and has a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 用于颜料或墨水的着色物质；只是拼写相似，词源不同。

entries.definition: A contact language with a reduced grammar, used between speakers of different tongues; it sounds the same but is a separate word of uncertain origin.
entries.definitionCN: 语法简化的接触语言，供不同语言使用者交流；读音相同，却是另一个词，来历另有说法。

entries.definition: A stockier bird of the same family, often white and used as a symbol of peace.
entries.definitionCN: 同科中体形更敦实的鸟，常为白色，被用作和平的象征。

entries.definition: A small brown city bird that also gathers wherever people scatter food.
entries.definitionCN: 城市里常见的小型褐色鸟，也会聚在有人撒食的地方。

entries.definition: A person who is easily deceived or used by others.
entries.definitionCN: 容易被欺骗、被他人利用的人。

entries.definition: The disc thrown into the air for shooting practice, whether or not the bird name is used.
entries.definitionCN: 为射击练习抛向空中的圆盘，用不用鸟名来称呼都可以。

normalIntro.en: A chirping nestling, a French diminutive and a set of English compounds carry the bird from the dovecote to the shooting range and to slang.
normalIntro.cn: 一个啾啾叫的雏鸟、一个法语指小形式，再加一串英语复合词，把这种鸟从鸽舍一路带到射击场，也带进了俚语。

normal.en: Pipio in Latin was a chirping young bird, so the word began as a description of a sound rather than the name of a species.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pipio 指会叫的幼鸟，所以这个词最初描述的是声音，而不是某一物种的名称。

normal.en: Old French kept the soft j, and English first wrote pijon before settling on pigeon.
normal.cn: 古法语保留了这个软音 j，英语先写作 pijon，后来才定为 pigeon。

normal.en: Pigeonhole started as a nesting niche in a dovecote and now names any small compartment and the act of filing something away.
normal.cn: pigeonhole 本是鸽舍里的巢格，如今指任何小格子，也指把东西归档搁置的动作。

normal.en: Carrier pigeon and homing pigeon are fixed compounds; the bird's real talent is returning home, not delivering letters by itself.
normal.cn: 信鸽与归巢鸽都是固定的复合说法；这种鸟真正的本事是认路回家，而不是自己送信。

normal.en: Pigeon-toed compares a person's turned-in feet to the bird's gait and is usually mildly mocking.
normal.cn: pigeon-toed 把人的内八字脚比作这种鸟的步态，通常带点取笑的意味。

abstract.en: A bird that lives on stone: the pigeon is the animal that turned a city into a cliff.
abstract.cn: 一只靠石头过日子的鸟：鸽子是把城市当成悬崖的那种动物。

abstract.en: The same word names the bird and the person who is fooled, as if tameness of body and trust of mind were one quality.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指这种鸟，也指上当的人，仿佛身体的驯服与心里的轻信是同一种品质。

abstract.en: Clay pigeons are named for what they are not: the target copies the flight, never the body.
abstract.cn: 泥鸽靶是用它「不是」的东西命名的：靶子复制的是飞行，从来不是身体。

examples.en: A grey pigeon pecked at the crumbs near the fountain.
examples.cn: 一只灰鸽在喷泉边啄食面包屑。

examples.en: He keeps a dozen pigeons on the roof and races them each spring.
examples.cn: 他在屋顶养了十几只鸽子，每年春天都拿它们比赛。

examples.en: The clay pigeon burst into dust as soon as the shot rang out.
examples.cn: 枪声一响，泥鸽靶就炸成了粉末。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮紧」——鸽子落在肩上，皮紧了一下才发觉；pigeon 就是鸽子。

root: 拉丁语 pipio（会啾啾叫的幼鸟，源自拟声动词 pipire，更早来源不确定）经古法语 pijon 进入英语；同族词多与这种鸟及其驯养用途有关。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins with a cheeping nestling, widens to the grey bird of the square, then narrows again to the trained bird, the fooled person and the clay disc.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从一只啾啾叫的雏鸟开始，放宽到广场上的灰鸟，又收窄到被驯养的鸟、上当的人，以及那个黏土圆盘。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flock of grey birds dropping onto a square, pecking, then lifting as one when a step comes too near.
core.cn: 核心意象：广场上一群灰鸽落地啄食，脚步一近就整片飞起。

branches.en: crumbs scattered beside a park bench
branches.cn: 长椅边撒开的面包屑

branches.en: a rooftop loft with a wire door
branches.cn: 屋顶上装着铁丝门的鸽舍

branches.en: a man counting coins for a watch that does not work
branches.cn: 有人为一块坏表数出硬币

branches.en: a clay disc spinning against the sky
branches.cn: 一只黏土圆盘在天空下旋转

branches.en: a tame bird and a trusting man, both easy to catch
branches.cn: 驯熟的鸟与轻信的人，都好捉

intro.en: An imitative Latin verb, its noun for a nestling, a French form and a set of English compounds hold the word together.
intro.cn: 一个拟声的拉丁动词、由它而来的雏鸟名词、一个法语词形和一串英语复合词，共同撑起这个词。

latinIntro.en: Only the verb of chirping and its noun are Latin; the bird's modern English name was shaped in French before English took it over.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语只提供了那个拟声动词和它的名词；这种鸟的现代英语名称是先在法语里成形，再由英语接手的。

items.meaning: a small compartment, a filing slot
a pigeon bred to return home
a clay disc used as a shooting target
items.meaningCN: 用作射击靶的黏土圆盘

definition_zh: 堆；一摞；桩；大量；堆积；堆放
definition_en: a quantity of things lying one on top of another, a heavy post driven into the ground, or the act of putting things into such a heap
core_image: 门口脱下的球鞋一只压一只，堆成一摞歪斜的鞋山
scene: 雨天的宿舍门口，湿透的球鞋一只叠一只，谁也不肯把它们摆正。A pile of wet boots had grown beside the door since morning.
sceneCN: 这里是「堆、一摞」（第 1 个义项：同类物件随意叠放成的一堆）；句意为从早上起门边就积起了一堆湿靴子。画面里是那摞越歪越高的鞋。

derivatives.zh: 由 pile 与 up 复合而成的名词，指多车追尾相撞的事故，也指事情的积压
由 pile 与 driver 复合而成，指把桩打进地里的机械
由 pile 加 -ing 构成的名词，指成排打入地下的桩或打桩工程

senses.title: A heap of things set one on another
senses.definition: a number of things lying on top of one another in a rough heap
senses.definitionCN: 若干物件随意地一层层叠放在一起形成的堆
senses.example: He left a pile of newspapers beside the chair.
senses.exampleCN: 他在椅子旁留下一摞报纸。
senses.why: This sense comes through Old French from Latin pila, a pillar or pier, because the earliest heaps in the record were stone masses built up like a support rather than loose scatter.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项经古法语上溯到拉丁语 pila（柱子、桥墩）：文献里最早的 pile 指像支柱一样垒起来的石堆，起点是「垒高的实体」，而不是散乱的东西。

senses.title: A heavy post driven into the ground
senses.definition: a long heavy post of timber, steel or concrete hammered into the ground to carry a building or a bridge
senses.definitionCN: 打入地下以承载建筑或桥梁的长而粗的木、钢或混凝土柱
senses.example: The workers drove the last pile into the river bed before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 天亮前工人们把最后一根桩打进了河床。
senses.why: This sense is a homonym from a different Latin word, pilum, a javelin or pointed stake; what carried over into engineering is its straight, pointed shape, not the idea of a heap.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项是同形异源，来自另一个拉丁词 pilum（标枪、尖桩）；被工程沿用下来的是它「直而尖、能砸进土里」的形状，而不是「堆」的念头。

senses.title: To put things into a heap
senses.definition: to put things one on top of another, often quickly and without much order
senses.definitionCN: 把东西一层层放上去，常是快速而不太整齐地
senses.example: She piled the dishes by the sink and went back for more.
senses.exampleCN: 她把盘子摞在水槽边，又回去端更多。
senses.why: Once the noun names a heap, the verb only has to name the act of producing one, and English regularly turns such mass nouns straight into verbs without adding anything.
senses.whyCN: 名词既然已指一摞东西，动词就只需指「造出这一摞」的动作；英语常把这类表示成堆之物的名词直接当动词用，不添任何词尾。

senses.title: A large amount, informally
senses.definition: a large number or amount of something, used in the fixed phrases a pile of and piles of
senses.definitionCN: 数量很多的某物，用于「a pile of」与「piles of」这类固定说法
senses.example: We still have piles of letters to answer.
senses.exampleCN: 我们还有成堆的信要回。
senses.why: A heap that stands tall is also a heap that holds much, so speakers took its height as a measure of quantity and let the plural stand for many.
senses.whyCN: 堆得高同时意味着装得多，说话人干脆用它的高度来量数量，让复数形式代表「许多」。

intro.en: English pile joins three Latin words that happen to look alike; the heap and the driven post are the two that shape everyday use.
intro.cn: 英语的 pile 把三个恰好长得相像的拉丁词并到了一起；其中真正塑造日常用法的是「堆」与「打入地下的桩」这两支。

items.en: Pila named a pillar, a pier or a stone barrier, and it is generally taken as the source of the French word for a heap.
items.cn: pila 指柱子、桥墩或石垒的屏障；一般认为它就是法语中表示「堆」的那个词的来源。

items.en: Pilum was a javelin, a pointed throwing spear, and it lies behind the sense of a stake driven into the ground.
items.cn: pilum 是标枪，一种带尖的投掷长矛，正是「打入地下的桩」这一义项的来源。

items.en: Old English borrowed the word as pil, a stake or post, so the post sense is older in English than the heap sense.
items.cn: 古英语借入这个词写作 pil，意为桩、柱，因此「桩」义在英语里比「堆」义更早。

items.en: Old French pile meant both a stone pier and a heap, and English took the heap meaning in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 pile 同时指石砌的桥墩与堆，英语在十五世纪接过了「堆」的意思。

items.en: Modern English adds the verb, the informal measure of a large amount, and compounds such as pile driver and pileup.
items.cn: 现代英语又添上动词用法、口语中表示大量的一种量法，以及打桩机、连环相撞这类复合词。

note.en: The first group gathers relatives of the Latin stems and the compounds built on the word; the second gathers the everyday words for a heap and for an upright post.
note.cn: 第一组收同一拉丁词干的同族词以及由这个词构成的复合词；第二组收日常里表示「堆」和「立柱」的词。

entries.definition: A set of piles driven into the ground, and also the -ing form of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 打入地下的一排桩，同时也是该动词的 -ing 形式。

entries.definition: A crash involving several vehicles, or a mass of things that has accumulated.
entries.definitionCN: 多车连环相撞的事故，或积压起来的一堆事物。

entries.definition: A tall upright support, from the same Latin pila that gave the heap sense.
entries.definitionCN: 高而直立的支撑物，与「堆」义同出拉丁语 pila。

entries.definition: A shallow decorative column set into a wall, also built on pila.
entries.definitionCN: 嵌入墙面的装饰性扁柱，同样建于 pila 之上。

entries.definition: A messy pile of things, the closest everyday synonym of the heap sense.
entries.definitionCN: 杂乱堆起的一堆东西，是「堆」义最贴近的日常同义词。

entries.definition: A neat pile arranged in regular layers, one on another.
entries.definitionCN: 整齐分层、一层压一层码放的摞。

entries.definition: A rounded raised mass, especially of earth.
entries.definitionCN: 圆隆凸起的一堆，尤指土堆。

entries.definition: A strong upright piece of wood or metal fixed in the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 固定在地里的坚固木柱或金属柱。

normalIntro.en: Two Latin stems and one English habit of turning nouns into verbs let a stone support become a heap, a heap become a verb, and a javelin become a post.
normalIntro.cn: 两个拉丁词干，加上英语把名词直接当动词用的习惯，让石砌的支撑变成堆，让堆变成动词，也让标枪变成桩。

normal.en: Pila in Latin was a pillar, so the first piles in English were heaps built up like a support rather than things simply thrown down.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pila 是柱子，所以英语里最早的 pile 是像支柱一样垒起来的堆，而不是随手倒下的东西。

normal.en: Pilum was a javelin, and its straight pointed shape survives in the engineering pile driven into a river bed.
normal.cn: pilum 是标枪，它直而尖的形状留在打进河床的工程桩上。

normal.en: The verb needs no new form: pile up simply sets the noun in motion.
normal.cn: 动词不必另造形状：pile up 只是让那个名词动起来。

normal.en: A pile of takes a singular noun and piles of takes a plural or an uncountable one, and both mean a lot.
normal.cn: a pile of 后面跟单数名词，piles of 后面跟复数或不可数名词，两者都表示很多。

normal.en: The past tense is piled with a single l, and the -ing form is piling, with the e dropped.
normal.cn: 过去式写作 piled，只有一个 l；加 -ing 时去掉 e，写作 piling。

abstract.en: A pile is order made by gravity alone: nobody arranged it, yet it holds a shape.
abstract.cn: 一堆东西只是重力做出来的秩序：没人整理过，它却有自己的形状。

abstract.en: The same letters name a heap and a post because English spelling merges accidents; the two meanings never grew from one another.
abstract.cn: 同样几个字母既指堆又指桩，只因英语拼写把偶然并到了一起；这两个意思并不是从一个长出来的。

abstract.en: Piles of work are counted like stones, and that is how a physical heap turns into a feeling of pressure.
abstract.cn: 成堆的工作像石头一样被数着，一堆实物就这样变成了一种压力的感觉。

examples.en: A pile of dry leaves had gathered against the fence.
examples.cn: 一堆干叶子积在篱笆边。

examples.en: They piled the boxes in the corridor and left without a word.
examples.cn: 他们把箱子堆在走廊里，一句话没说就走了。

examples.en: He drove the first pile into the mud at low tide.
examples.cn: 退潮时他把第一根桩打进了泥里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派欧」——快递派送时把包裹往门口一堆，越派越欧（多）；pile 就是堆。

root: 「堆」义经古法语 pile 上溯到拉丁语 pila（柱子、桥墩），「桩」义来自拉丁语 pilum（标枪）经古英语 pil；另有拉丁语 pilus（毛发）一派，三者在英语中同形。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts from a stone support, becomes the heap leaning against it, then the act of heaping, the height that measures plenty, and finally the post hammered into a river bed.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从石砌的支撑开始，变成靠着它的那堆东西，再变成堆东西的动作、用高度来量的「许多」，最后是砸进河床的桩。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: boots left at a door, each one dropped on the one before, until they lean into a crooked stack.
